The collaboration with NVIDIA aims to enhance DreamDrive Pro's capabilities, delivering continuous improvements and a future-ready customer experience through software updates.

title: Nvidia debuts next-generation H100 GPUs, its most powerful chips yet
summary: Nvidia has unveiled its next-generation H100 GPUs, built on the new Hopper architecture, which promise an order of magnitude performance improvement over previous models. These chips feature 80 billion transistors, a Transformer Engine for accelerating AI language models, and HBM3 memory. The H100 GPUs are designed for advanced AI workloads, including real-time inference, and will be available to customers and cloud providers in the third quarter.

title: NVIDIA Launches AI Computing Platform for Medical Devices and Computational Sensing Systems
summary: NVIDIA has introduced Clara Holoscan MGX, an AI computing platform designed for the medical device industry to develop and deploy real-time AI applications at the edge, adhering to regulatory standards. This platform expands the existing Clara Holoscan framework, offering a medical-grade reference architecture and long-term software support. It aims to accelerate innovation in medical devices by enabling real-time insights from high-throughput data streams for applications like robotic surgery and drug discovery.

title: Keynote Wrap-Up: Turning Data Centers into ‘AI Factories,’ NVIDIA CEO Intros Hopper Architecture, H100 GPU, New Supercomputers, Software
summary: During NVIDIA GTC, CEO Jensen Huang unveiled a vision of data centers as "AI Factories," introducing the new Hopper GPU architecture and H100 GPU, along with new AI and accelerated computing software. He also announced powerful new data-center-scale systems, including Grace CPU Superchip and DGX H100 supercomputers. Huang emphasized the role of Omniverse in integrating real and virtual worlds, speeding collaboration, and serving as a proving ground for new robotics and autonomous vehicles.

title: Siemens Gamesa Taps NVIDIA Digital Twin Platform for Scientific Computing to Accelerate Clean Energy Transition
summary: Siemens Gamesa is collaborating with NVIDIA to develop physics-informed digital twins of wind farms using NVIDIA Omniverse and NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo. This digital twin platform for scientific computing aims to optimize wind farm layouts, increase electricity production, and reduce operating costs by enabling faster and more accurate simulations of computational fluid dynamics, up to 4,000 times quicker than traditional methods. The technology will help analyze and minimize wake effects between turbines, accelerating the clean energy transition.

title: NVIDIA Announces DGX H100 Systems – World’s Most Advanced Enterprise AI Infrastructure
summary: NVIDIA has announced its fourth-generation DGX H100 systems, which are the world's first AI platforms built with the new NVIDIA H100 Tensor Core GPUs, offering 32 petaflops of AI performance. These systems are foundational for the next-generation DGX POD and DGX SuperPOD AI infrastructure, with the latter able to deliver 1 exaflop of AI performance. NVIDIA is also building the "Eos" supercomputer, which is expected to be the world's fastest AI system with 18.4 exaflops of AI computing performance, set to begin operations later this year.

title: NVIDIA Introduces Grace CPU Superchip
summary: NVIDIA has unveiled its Grace CPU Superchip, an Arm Neoverse-based discrete data center CPU engineered for AI infrastructure and high-performance computing. This new chip boasts 144 high-performance cores and 1 terabyte/second memory, offering double the performance and energy-efficiency compared to current leading server chips. It is designed to work seamlessly with NVIDIA's existing software stacks and is expected to be available in the first half of 2023.

title: NVIDIA Opens NVLink for Custom Silicon Integration
summary: NVIDIA has announced the opening of NVLink-C2C, an ultra-fast chip-to-chip and die-to-die interconnect, for custom silicon integration. This technology allows coherent interconnection between custom dies and NVIDIA's GPUs, CPUs, and DPUs, offering significant improvements in energy efficiency and area efficiency compared to PCIe Gen 5. It supports industry standards like Arm AMBA CHI and will also be compatible with the developing Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express (UCIe) standard, providing options for custom silicon integration with NVIDIA chips.

title: NVIDIA Launches Data-Center-Scale Omniverse Computing System for Industrial Digital Twins
summary: NVIDIA has introduced OVX, a new computing system designed to power large-scale industrial digital twins within its Omniverse platform. OVX combines high-performance GPU-accelerated compute, graphics, and AI with fast storage and networking to create physically accurate simulations for complex applications. This system will enable industries to build and test digital twins of factories, cities, and railway networks, and is expected to be available later this year through partners like Inspur, Lenovo, and Supermicro.

title: NVIDIA Announces Availability of Jetson AGX Orin Developer Kit to Advance Robotics and Edge AI
summary: NVIDIA has announced the availability of its Jetson AGX Orin developer kit, a powerful AI supercomputer designed for advanced robotics, autonomous machines, and edge computing. This new kit offers over eight times the processing power of its predecessor, the Jetson AGX Xavier, while maintaining a compact form factor. NVIDIA expects the Jetson AGX Orin to accelerate the development of next-generation robotics and edge AI products across various industries, supported by a broad ecosystem of partners and customers.

title: Lucid Announces Integration of Its Proprietary DreamDrive Pro Advanced Driver-Assistance System with NVIDIA DRIVE Hyperion Software-Defined Platform
summary: Lucid Group announced the integration of its DreamDrive Pro advanced driver-assistance system with NVIDIA DRIVE Hyperion software-defined platform. This collaboration ensures that DreamDrive Pro will gain new capabilities over time through over-the-air software updates, leveraging NVIDIA's powerful compute architecture. The system, featuring a 32-sensor suite, is already integrated into every Lucid Air and is designed for future enhancements.

title: NVIDIA Launches Omniverse for Developers: A Powerful and Collaborative Game Creation Environment
summary: NVIDIA has launched new Omniverse features for developers, creating a powerful and collaborative environment for game creation. This update streamlines game development by integrating AI and NVIDIA RTX tools, enabling real-time collaboration and enhancing character animation and asset management. Key new features include Omniverse Audio2Face, Omniverse Nucleus Cloud, Omniverse DeepSearch, and an Unreal Engine 5 Omniverse Connector.

title: NVIDIA Announces Hopper Architecture, the Next Generation of Accelerated Computing
summary: NVIDIA has announced its next-generation accelerated computing platform, NVIDIA Hopper architecture, featuring the new H100 GPU with 80 billion transistors. This architecture delivers an order of magnitude performance leap over its predecessor, the Ampere architecture, and includes groundbreaking features such as a Transformer Engine and scalable NVLink for advanced AI models. The H100, designed for "AI factories," is expected to be available later this year from leading cloud service providers and computer makers.

title: NVIDIA DRIVE Continues Industry Momentum With $11 Billion Pipeline as DRIVE Orin Enters Production
summary: NVIDIA's DRIVE Hyperion platform, powered by DRIVE Orin, is gaining significant industry momentum with an $11 billion automotive pipeline. Leading EV maker BYD and several self-driving startups have selected the DRIVE Hyperion architecture for their next-generation software-defined vehicles, with DRIVE Orin now in production. The platform enables advanced autonomous driving capabilities and supports the development of new energy vehicles.

title: Introducing NVIDIA DRIVE Hyperion 9: Next-Generation Platform for Software-Defined Autonomous Vehicle Fleets
summary: NVIDIA announced DRIVE Hyperion 9, its next-generation open platform for automated and autonomous vehicles, set to launch in 2027. This scalable and programmable architecture will leverage the DRIVE Thor central computer, offering 8x the performance of current platforms. DRIVE Hyperion 9 features heightened sensing capabilities with a rich array of high-resolution cameras, radars, lidars, and ultrasonics, designed for Level 3 urban and Level 4 highway driving.

title: This tech group is leading the charge in sustainable Web 3.0 development
summary: Atlas Technology Management, a Singapore-headquartered technology group, is expanding its Web 3.0 computing infrastructure and committing to sustainable development. The company aims to achieve 100% green energy adoption by 2024 and plans to expand its global coverage to over 30 countries in the next five years. Atlas is also exploring advanced technologies like underwater data centers to minimize environmental impact.

title: Nvidia CEO says interested in exploring chip manufacturing with Intel
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang expressed interest in exploring Intel's chip manufacturing services. Intel, which aims to expand its foundry business, confirmed ongoing discussions with Nvidia. This potential collaboration could be significant for Intel's efforts to attract external chip design companies to its factories.

title: Kroger partners with Nvidia to boost freshness efforts using AI
summary: Kroger has announced a strategic collaboration with Nvidia to enhance its fresh food initiatives using artificial intelligence and online simulations. The partnership will establish a lab and demonstration center at Kroger's headquarters to develop AI-driven methods for identifying food spoilage, optimizing delivery routes, and improving in-store efficiency. This move aims to leverage technology to extend the shelf life of fresh produce and improve customer service, aligning with Kroger's "Fresh for Everyone" branding.

title: Kroger launches ambitious AI transformation program
summary: Kroger is launching an ambitious AI transformation program through a partnership with Nvidia, aiming to enhance enterprise operations. This initiative includes building an AI lab and demonstration center to improve freshness initiatives, shipping logistics, and store experiences using digital twin simulations. Kroger will also leverage technologies like computer vision and dynamic routing for last-mile delivery, building on its existing AI-driven fulfillment model with Ocado.

title: Possible Nvidia, Intel GPU Alliance Could Frustrate Rivals AMD, TSMC
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is in talks with Intel to use its foundries for GPU production, a move that could significantly impact competitors AMD and TSMC. This potential alliance would diversify Nvidia's supply base and challenge TSMC's dominance in the foundry market, while also putting pressure on AMD's supercomputing ambitions. Both Intel and Nvidia are interested in the collaboration, with Intel aiming to become the top GPU foundry by 2025.

title: Nvidia considers teaming up with Intel on chip manufacturing
summary: Nvidia is in discussions with Intel about potentially using Intel as a foundry for manufacturing its chips. This consideration comes amid a global semiconductor chip shortage and Intel's efforts to become a major U.S. foundry supplier, despite the challenges of aligning technologies and business models between the companies. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang expressed openness to the idea, noting existing close collaboration between the firms.

title: 16-year-old living with his mom is Lapsus$ mastermind behind Microsoft hack, cyber detectives say
summary: Cybersecurity researchers have traced a string of hacks against major technology companies like Microsoft, Nvidia, and Okta to a 16-year-old living with his mother near Oxford, England. This teenager, known online as "White" and "breachbase," is believed to be the mastermind behind the Lapsus$ hacking group, which has engaged in social engineering and extortion campaigns, often taunting victims and recruiting insiders. The group, which Microsoft tracks as "DEV-0537," is known for its poor operational security, allowing researchers to gain insights into its members who also include a suspected teenager in Brazil.

title: SoftBank preps Arm IPO, seeking a $60B valuation
summary: SoftBank is preparing for an Initial Public Offering (IPO) of Arm Ltd., aiming for a $60 billion valuation, following the collapse of its proposed sale to Nvidia Corp. The valuation is considered ambitious but potentially realistic due to Nvidia's appreciating stock price since the original acquisition agreement. Analysts suggest the success of the IPO at this valuation could indicate investor confidence in Arm's own growth potential beyond a merger.

title: WeRide zooms to $400m
summary: China-based autonomous driving technology producer WeRide has raised $400 million from investors including GAC and Robert Bosch, bringing its valuation to $4.4 billion. This latest funding round increases the company's total funding to over $1.2 billion and follows previous rounds with notable investors such as Alliance Ventures and Nvidia GPU Ventures. WeRide, founded in 2017, develops software and hardware for level 4 autonomous driving.

title: Columbia Threadneedle Investments launches Columbia Seligman Semiconductor and Technology ETF
summary: Columbia Threadneedle Investments has launched its first actively managed, semi-transparent ETF, the Columbia Seligman Semiconductor and Technology ETF (SEMI). Managed by Paul Wick and his team, SEMI focuses on growth within the semiconductor and related technology sectors, investing in 30 to 50 companies. The fund aims to capitalize on the critical role of semiconductors in modern technologies and offers investors exposure to a sector believed to be reasonably valued with strong potential for future returns.

title: TIME100 Most Influential Companies 2022: NVIDIA
summary: NVIDIA, under CEO Jensen Huang, has become critical for various technologies from cryptocurrency to self-driving cars, earning it a spot on the 2022 TIME100 Most Influential Companies list. Despite abandoning a major acquisition, NVIDIA's investments in AI and experimental technology are profoundly shaping the future, with expectations for its processors to make human effort obsolete in many sectors.

title: TIME100 Most Influential Companies 2022: NVIDIA
summary: NVIDIA has been recognized as one of TIME's 100 Most Influential Companies of 2022 due to its essential role in advancing technology. Under CEO Jensen Huang, NVIDIA's processors are crucial for cryptocurrency, NFTs, and self-driving cars. The company's investments in AI and experimental technology are significantly shaping the future, despite abandoning a major acquisition this year.

title: The semiconductor decade: A trillion-dollar industry
summary: The global semiconductor industry is projected to reach a trillion-dollar valuation by 2030, driven by an average annual growth rate of 6 to 8 percent. Key growth areas include automotive, computation and data storage, and wireless technologies, with automotive expected to triple demand. Industry leaders are advised to strategically focus on R&D, manufacturing, and sourcing to capitalize on this expansion.

title: TSMC To Become NVIDIA’s Sole GPU Supplier In 2022 – Report
summary: A report from Business Korea suggests that TSMC is poised to become NVIDIA's sole GPU supplier by the end of 2022 due to ongoing issues with Samsung Foundry's production yields. NVIDIA, which previously diversified its suppliers, is now reportedly moving all its GPU manufacturing to TSMC, including its new Hopper data center GPUs. This shift follows earlier rumors of a rift between Samsung and NVIDIA and significant investments by NVIDIA into TSMC's advanced manufacturing processes.

title: Corsair One i300 review
summary: The Corsair One i300 is a compact and stylish small form factor gaming PC that offers extremely high-end performance with components like the Intel Core i9-12900K and Nvidia GeForce RTX 3080 Ti. While it excels in performance for 4K gaming and also serves as a powerful workstation for content creators, its major drawbacks are its exorbitant price tag ($4,999 / £4,399) and limited upgradeability due to its small chassis. The review concludes that while it's a top-tier machine for those who can afford it and don't plan on tinkering, it's overkill and too expensive for most casual gamers.

title: Investing in esports in the context of recent events
summary: This article discusses the growth of esports, significant investment it has received, and current challenges due to global events like the COVID-19 pandemic and the Russia-Ukraine conflict. It identifies investment opportunities in publicly traded tech companies, specialized esports firms, and esports-focused ETFs, while also raising questions about future growth amidst potential new pandemics and the integration of NFTs.

title: Baidu Proposes PP-YOLOE: An Evolved Version of YOLO that Achieves SOTA Performance in Object Detection
summary: Baidu researchers have introduced PP-YOLOE, an evolved version of the YOLO object detector, which demonstrates state-of-the-art performance in object detection. This new model surpasses previous versions like YOLOX and PP-YOLOv2 in both speed and accuracy on COCO datasets. The improvements stem from architectural optimizations, an anchor-free method, novel RepResBlock usage, task alignment learning, and an Efficient Task-aligned Head.

title: New IBM Z mainframe blunts quantum cyber attacks
summary: IBM has introduced its latest Z mainframe system, featuring a new Telum processor with a built-in AI accelerator. This system is designed to enhance AI inferencing capabilities for financial transactions, enabling real-time fraud analysis. Additionally, it incorporates advanced security measures, including quantum-safe cryptography, to defend against cyberattacks from quantum computers.

title: Technology ETF
summary: VanEck offers a suite of Technology ETFs that allow investors to gain exposure to disruptive and transformative megatrends such as semiconductors, spatial technology, hydrogen, esports, and cryptocurrency. These ETFs provide diversified exposure, potential for future winners through rules-based selection, regular rebalancing, and lower fees compared to actively managed funds. The article also details various risks associated with investing in Technology ETFs, including industry concentration, market risk, and liquidity risks.

title: Hello FPGA – Getting Started with Microchip FPGAs
summary: The "Hello FPGA" webinar introduces Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) and Microchip's low-power FPGA portfolio, drawing from a Microchip University course. It covers fundamental FPGA technology, provides background information, and features videos from the course, guided by Tim McCarthy (Microchip) and Clemens Valens (Elektor). The webinar aims to make FPGAs more accessible, despite their perceived complexity requiring hardware description languages like VHDL or Verilog.

title: Experts Details: Lillian Currens
summary: This page provides details about Lillian Currens, the deputy editor at Schaeffer's Investment Research. It highlights her professional background, experience in writing and editing digital content, and her role in managing Schaeffer's social media. The article also lists several of her published articles discussing stock analyses for companies like Netflix, Vertex Pharmaceuticals, Nvidia, and Home Depot.

title: Meta (FB) Plans to Introduce Virtual Coins to Diversify Income
summary: Meta Platforms (FB) is exploring the introduction of virtual coins, tokens, and lending services within its applications to reduce its reliance on advertising revenue. The company plans to create in-app tokens, similar to those in games like Roblox, and also social tokens and "creator coins" for influencers, rather than a blockchain-based cryptocurrency like its failed Diem project. This strategic shift aims to diversify its income streams and engage users amidst increasing competition and regulatory scrutiny.

title: Which is the bigger company: AMD, Nvidia, or Intel?
summary: This article analyzes Intel, AMD, and Nvidia to determine which is the "bigger" company, looking beyond market capitalization to factors like employee count, revenue, product diversity, and market share. While Nvidia leads in market cap, sustained analysis reveals Intel to be the largest overall due to its revenue and employee numbers, despite AMD and Nvidia's significant recent growth. The article also touches on the unique advantage Intel holds with its chip manufacturing capabilities.

title: Metaverse Market Size [2022-2029] Worth USD 1527.55 Billion | Exhibiting a CAGR of 47.6%
summary: The metaverse market is projected to grow significantly from USD 100.27 billion in 2022 to USD 1,527.55 billion by 2029, showcasing a CAGR of 47.6%. This growth is primarily driven by the increasing penetration of online shopping and gaming, alongside advancements in blockchain technology and VR devices. Key companies leading this expansion include Tencent Holdings Ltd., NVIDIA Corporation, Meta, and Microsoft Corporation, who are focusing on product portfolio expansion and technological innovation.

title: NVIDIA enters Top 5 of Fortune's '100 Best Companies to Work For'
summary: NVIDIA has been ranked #5 on Fortune's 2022 list of the "100 Best Companies to Work For," placing ahead of major financial institutions like Capital One and American Express. Cisco secured the top spot for the second consecutive year, followed by Hilton and Wegmans Food Markets, Inc., with Salesforce coming in fourth. The recognition highlights the importance of strong workplace culture during a period of significant workforce changes.

title: These 4 Houston companies are honored as Fortune’s 100 Best Companies to Work For
summary: Four Houston-based companies, including David Weekley Homes, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, Camden Property Trust, and Hilcorp, have been recognized on Fortune's 2022 100 Best Companies to Work For list. David Weekley Homes notably secured a top 10 spot, ranking No. 9, while other Texas companies also made the list. The rankings were determined by Great Place to Work, surveying employees on trust, care, and fairness.

title: Ensuring a stronger US-Taiwan tech supply chain partnership
summary: This article discusses the importance of strengthening the US-Taiwan tech supply chain partnership, particularly in the semiconductor industry, amidst increasing global geopolitical polarization. It highlights the challenges of meeting chip demands, cultivating engineering talent, and the need for comprehensive integration beyond just manufacturing. The piece advocates for policy clarity, R&D collaborations, and deeper economic integration to ensure mutual benefit and resilience for both the US and Taiwan.

title: The end of one-chip wonders: Why Nvidia, Intel and AMD's valuations have experienced massive upheaval
summary: The semiconductor industry has seen a dramatic shift, with Nvidia now valued as much as Intel and AMD combined, a reversal from five years ago when Intel held that position. This change reflects evolving technology interaction and other companies specializing in new areas, causing Intel to fall behind. The article highlights a massive upheaval in semiconductor valuations mirroring the industry's transformation.

title: The end of one-chip wonders: Why Nvidia, Intel and AMD’s valuations have experienced massive upheaval
summary: The article discusses the dramatic shift in valuations among semiconductor companies, specifically Nvidia, Intel, and AMD. Five years ago, Intel's market capitalization surpassed Nvidia and AMD combined, but now Nvidia alone is worth more than the other two combined, reflecting significant changes in the semiconductor industry. This upheaval is attributed to evolving technology consumption patterns and companies specializing in new areas.

title: The end of one-chip wonders: Why Nvidia, Intel and AMD’s valuations have experienced massive upheaval
summary: This article discusses the dramatic shift in market capitalization within the semiconductor industry over the past five years. Once dominant Intel has been surpassed by Nvidia, which is now valued as much as Intel and AMD combined, reflecting fundamental changes in how technology is used and specialized solutions. This upheaval highlights a significant transformation in the industry's landscape.

title: Micron Commences Volume Production of 16 Gb GDDR6X Memory For NVIDIA’s RTX 3090 Ti, Also Readies 24 Gbps GDDR6X Dies For Future Graphics Cards
summary: Micron has begun volume production of its 16Gb GDDR6X memory, which is now integrated into NVIDIA's GeForce RTX 3090 Ti graphics card, offering twice the capacity and up to 15% higher performance than its predecessor. The company is also developing 24 Gbps GDDR6X memory dies to enhance performance in future graphics cards, supporting speeds up to 24Gb/s. This advancement leverages Micron's PAM4 signal techniques for improved power efficiency and bandwidth, critical for demanding applications like 4K/8K gaming and 3D CAD.

title: With Vast Data, Nvidia is in the company of a storage unicorn
summary: Nvidia has deepened its relationship with storage unicorn Vast Data, with Nvidia Bluefield DPUs now powering Vast Data's new Ceres storage platform. This collaboration aims to redefine data center storage for the AI era by leveraging advanced flash drives and DPU technology for improved performance and cost efficiency. The partnership evolved through Mellanox, which Nvidia acquired and had previously invested in Vast Data, and both companies are also developing Zero Trust access to data storage and GPU direct storage.

title: Broadcom Inc. stock falls Thursday, underperforms market
summary: Broadcom Inc. (AVGO) stock fell 3.15% on Thursday, closing at $573.85, a day when the broader market also saw declines. This drop ended a two-day winning streak for the company, leaving its stock $103.91 short of its 52-week high. Competitors such as Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. Ltd. ADR, NVIDIA Corp., and Intel Corp. also experienced declines.

title: Synopsys Introduces Industry's Highest Performance Neural Processor IP
summary: Synopsys has launched its DesignWare ARC NPX6 and NPX6FS NPU IP, along with the MetaWare MX Development Toolkit, to meet the increasing performance demands of AI systems-on-chip. This new NPU IP delivers the industry's highest performance, offering up to 3,500 TOPS for AI applications and support for complex neural network models, while also addressing functional safety requirements for automotive use. The comprehensive software environment aims to accelerate application development and ensure compliance with standards like ISO 26262.

title: Nvidia's GPU-powered AI is creating chips with 'better than human design'
summary: Nvidia is leveraging its GPU-powered AI to develop and design new computer chips, including its own GPUs, leading to designs that are "better than human." The company's chief scientist, Bill Dally, explained how AI is used to accelerate chip design processes like power estimation, parasitic prediction, and automated standard cell migration. This approach not only significantly reduces design time and labor but also results in more efficient and smaller chip components, showcasing a win-win scenario for Nvidia's internal development and its AI hardware offerings.

title: Roundhill Cannabis ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (BATS:WEED) $WEED
summary: The Roundhill Cannabis ETF (BATS:WEED) is an actively managed exchange-traded fund that invests in global cannabis and hemp companies. Launched on April 20, 2022, the ETF has $9.73 million in assets under management and a net expense ratio of 0.00%. The article provides details on the ETF's holdings, price performance, key statistics, and recent news headlines.

title: Lapsus$ Cyberattack Victim List: Globant, Microsoft, Nvidia, Okta, Samsung, T-Mobile -
summary: The Lapsus$ hacker group continued to target high-profile companies even after some alleged members were arrested in March 2022. This article lists several major companies, including Globant, Microsoft, Nvidia, Okta, Samsung, and T-Mobile, that have been victims of Lapsus$ cyberattacks. It also provides guidance on how to protect against and respond to ransomware attacks, emphasizing data backups, multi-factor authentication, and prompt incident reporting.

title: Leaked Chats Show LAPSUS$ Stole T-Mobile Source Code – Krebs on Security
summary: Leaked private chat messages from the LAPSUS$ cybercrime group reveal they breached T-Mobile multiple times in March 2022, stealing source code for various projects. Despite T-Mobile's claim that no customer or government information was compromised, the chats detail LAPSUS$'s methods, including purchasing access, social engineering employees, and utilizing internal tools like Atlas to look up sensitive accounts. The article also highlights the group's internal conflicts, their leader's fixation on stealing source code, and their eventual undoing due to compromised servers and arrests.

title: Chipmaker Texas Instruments expects revenue hit as China lockdowns dent demand
summary: Texas Instruments (TXN.O) forecast second-quarter revenue below Wall Street estimates due to reduced demand caused by COVID-19 lockdowns in China, sending its shares down 7% in extended trading. The company noted that the impact was primarily due to disruptions at its customers' factories. Despite this, Texas Instruments reported a 14% revenue increase to $4.91 billion for the first quarter, exceeding analyst expectations.

title: Fidelity Enters the Metaverse with New Financial Education Experience: Invest Quest at The Fidelity Stack
summary: Fidelity Investments has launched a new gamified financial education experience called "The Fidelity Stack" in Decentraland, an eight-story virtual building designed to teach users about ETF investing through an "Invest Quest" challenge. This initiative aims to engage younger audiences, particularly the 18-35 age range, following the company's recent introduction of a metaverse-themed ETF, FMET. Fidelity views this as a significant step in providing financial education in decentralized, virtual communities.

title: HPE Creates Its Own AI Stack For Large Enterprises
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) is expanding its AI software portfolio and leveraging its HPC hardware expertise to provide a comprehensive AI stack for large enterprises. This initiative includes a Machine Learning Development System that simplifies infrastructure management and facilitates collaboration for training models at scale, addressing the complexities faced by data scientists. Furthermore, HPE is promoting "swarm learning" to enable AI model training where data resides, crucial for privacy and compliance in industries like healthcare and banking.

title: HCL Technologies brings All Access Media Marketplace Platform
summary: HCL Technologies has launched its All Access Media Marketplace Platform at NAB Las Vegas, aiming to streamline content creation and distribution processes. Developed in coordination with Microsoft and CoreSite, the platform addresses workflow, application, and vendor discovery challenges for media creators. It features HCL Workflow Creator for building workflows, leverages Microsoft 365 for communication, and utilizes Azure Cloud for cybersecurity, aligning with MovieLabs 2030 Vision.

title: Nvidia’s CFO on how they retain tech talent —even as the Great Resignation continues
summary: Colette Kress, Nvidia's CFO, discusses the company's strategies for retaining top tech talent amidst the Great Resignation. She emphasizes that beyond competitive salaries, a strong culture focused on continuous learning, challenging work, and an egalitarian leadership approach are key factors. Nvidia provides unique upskilling opportunities, offers benefits like "Free Days" and an employee stock purchase program, and fosters an environment where all employees are valued and have opportunities to lead, regardless of title.

title: US-based Applied Materials’ India arm buys office space, land in Bangalore for Rs 338 crore
summary: Applied Materials India, the subsidiary of the US-based semiconductor equipment manufacturer, has acquired nearly 10 acres of land and 2.6 lakh sq ft of office space in Bangalore for Rs 338 crore. This acquisition is part of the company's plan to invest over Rs 1,800 crore in India to expand its engineering infrastructure and support its growth. India is projected to become the fastest-growing semiconductor consumption market globally, with demand expected to exceed $110 billion by the end of the decade.

title: “There must be a new approach to the design of chips for high-performance computing applications”
summary: Joe Costello, former CEO of Cadence, has joined Anari AI as a Board Advisor to guide the startup in revolutionizing the hardware AI industry. Costello discusses the future of semiconductors, emphasizing the transition from general-purpose to domain-specific architectures, the critical role of cloud computing, and the transformative impact of AI/ML. He highlights the necessity of new chip design approaches for high-performance computing and the importance of fostering strong ecosystems.

title: Nvidia: transforming industries with pioneering AI tech
summary: Nvidia, a leader in AI and accelerated computing, is transforming industries through its pioneering technology. The company designs GPUs and APIs, supporting over 2.5 million developers globally and expanding its presence in gaming with RTX technology. Nvidia has also developed the Omniverse platform for virtual world simulation and is rapidly advancing supercomputing with its CUDA programming model and new H100 GPU and Grace CPU Superchip processors.

title: FMET Is a New, Fabulous Metaverse Idea
summary: Fidelity has launched the Fidelity Metaverse ETF (FMET), which tracks the Fidelity Metaverse Index, to capitalize on the nascent but expanding metaverse investment theme. The ETF mixes established tech giants with innovative smaller companies, including Meta Platforms, Apple, NVIDIA, Tencent, Baidu, and JD.com. Investors are advised that patience will be key for metaverse investing due to anticipated volatility, though the long-term growth outlook is considered bright with billions in projected revenue.

title: Toyota to apply artificial intelligence to boost efficiency in its factories
summary: Toyota Motor North America (TMNA) is partnering with Invisible AI to implement artificial intelligence in its factories to improve efficiency and safety. This AI system, using computer vision, will be deployed in 14 North American factories to analyze manufacturing operations, detect issues, and enhance processes. The initiative aims to reduce inefficiencies and ensures data privacy by analyzing information in-house and anonymizing videos to protect workers.

title: Nvidia fined $5.5M by SEC over failing to disclose crypto as revenue generator
summary: Nvidia has been fined $5.5 million by the SEC for failing to disclose that cryptomining was a significant revenue generator from its graphics processing units designed for gaming. The SEC stated that Nvidia deprived investors of critical information regarding the impact of volatile cryptocurrency sales on its business. Nvidia did not admit or deny the findings and has agreed to a cease-and-desist order.

title: Nvidia to pay $5.5 million penalty for 'inadequate disclosures' about cryptomining
summary: Nvidia Corporation has agreed to pay a $5.5 million civil penalty to settle charges from the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). The SEC alleged that Nvidia failed to adequately disclose the significant impact of cryptomining on its gaming revenue growth in fiscal 2018. The company did not admit or deny the findings but agreed to the settlement, which highlights its omission of information crucial for investors and analysts.

title: Nvidia pays $5.5m SEC fine over crypto-mining disclosures
summary: Nvidia agreed to pay a $5.5 million fine to the SEC for failing to adequately disclose revenue from crypto mining during two quarters in 2018. The SEC stated that Nvidia omitted information about surging demand from crypto miners while discussing how digital assets impacted other business lines. This lack of disclosure made Nvidia's financial results less predictable for investors.

title: Nvidia To Pay $5.5M Fine For Failing To Disclose GPU Cryptomining Sales: SEC
summary: Nvidia has been fined $5.5 million by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) for failing to disclose to investors that a significant portion of its 2018 GPU sales were driven by cryptocurrency mining. The SEC alleged that Nvidia misled investors and analysts, who were keenly interested in the impact of crypto mining on the company's gaming revenue. While Nvidia didn't admit wrongdoing, it agreed to pay the civil penalty.

title: NVIDIA (NVDA) Fined $5.5M for Failing to Disclose Crypto Mining Impact
summary: NVIDIA was fined $5.5 million by the SEC for failing to disclose the significant impact of cryptocurrency mining demand on its graphics card sales during fiscal year 2018. The SEC stated that this omission deprived investors of crucial information regarding the company's business in a key market. Following the settlement, NVIDIA's stock experienced a decline, reflecting the underperformance of its crypto mining processor (CMP) chips amid a downturn in cryptocurrency prices.

title: Why Marvell bought interconnect upstart Tanzanite
summary: Marvell Technology has acquired Tanzanite, a CXL startup specializing in memory expansion and pooling, to accelerate its composable infrastructure ambitions. The acquisition aims to disaggregate compute, memory, and storage resources, allowing them to be composed on the fly for memory-intensive workloads like AI/ML. While achieving fully composable data centers will take time, Marvell believes CXL technology will be crucial for integrating accelerators across its product portfolio and overcoming latency challenges associated with extending CXL benefits beyond server chassis.

summary: Intel Corp launched new AI chips, Gaudi2 and Greco, to challenge Nvidia's dominance in the AI chip market. summary: WeRide has launched a public pilot of 50 self-driving Robo Street Sweepers in Guangzhou, China, powered by NVIDIA technology. summary: Texas Instruments has broken ground on new 300-mm semiconductor wafer fabrication plants in Sherman, Texas, representing a potential $30 billion investment. summary: Nvidia projects a decline in video game chip sales for the current quarter and attributes new supply-chain challenges to China's COVID-19 lockdowns. summary: The article discusses the ongoing global supply chain crisis, examining its causes, current impact across various sectors like semiconductors, automobiles, industrials, retail, and restaurants, and potential timelines for recovery. CEO Jensen Huang highlighted four key initiatives: ramping next-generation AI infrastructure, launching the Grace CPU, expanding the ORIN robotics processor, and growing software platforms like Nvidia AI and Omniverse. Despite strong earnings that beat analyst expectations, the stock saw a dip in after-hours trading.

summary: NVIDIA announced that top global computer makers including Atos, Dell Technologies, GIGABYTE, HPE, Inspur, Lenovo, and Supermicro are adopting its new Grace and Grace Hopper superchips to build next-generation servers for AI and HPC workloads. summary: Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL) announced new details of its supercomputer collaboration with Nvidia and HPE, resulting in the "Venado" system. summary: NVIDIA is launching a new campaign to connect its diverse impacts across various fields, from gaming and AI to scientific research and business innovation. summary: Semiconductor stocks have seen significant declines in 2022, creating a strong buying opportunity for long-term investors. summary: Nvidia has updated its TAO Toolkit platform to simplify and accelerate deep learning model creation for enterprise applications, making AI development more accessible and less time-consuming. While other companies have also worked on simplifying AI pipelines, analysts note that Nvidia's TAO Toolkit, with its low-code nature and pre-trained models, aims to speed up time-to-market for AI models and reduce the need for extensive data science expertise.

summary: A former ASML engineer, Zongchang Yu, accused of stealing intellectual property, is now serving as CEO of XTAL Inc. in China. Despite lawsuits and a massive uncollectable fine against XTAL, Yu fled to China and reportedly runs DongFang with government support, benefiting from patents that include the contested OPC software.

title: OpenLight launches as fabless silicon photonics outfit

The company specializes in integrated on-chip lasers for high-performance photonic integrated circuits, using Tower Semiconductor's PH18DA fabrication process. OpenLight aims to overcome the challenge of integrating laser sources directly onto silicon photonics wafers, reducing costs and improving power efficiency for various applications like data communications, AI, and optical computing.

summary: Andrew Ng's startup, Landing AI, is leveraging his data-centric AI philosophy and NVIDIA GPUs to automate factory inspections, improving efficiency and reducing costs for manufacturers. summary: TSMC Chairman Mark Liu discusses how 5G, A.I., and high-performance computing (HPC) are ushering in a "golden era" for the semiconductor industry. title: Opinion | Semiconductor Dependency Imperils American Security
summary: The article argues that the U.S.'s heavy reliance on Taiwan for advanced semiconductor manufacturing poses a significant national security risk, particularly in light of potential Chinese dominance. A disruption in Taiwan's chip production could severely impact the U.S.

title: AI in the Big Easy: NVIDIA Research Lets Content Creators Improvise With 3D Objects
summary: NVIDIA Research has developed a new method called NVIDIA 3D MoMa, which allows content creators to quickly import 3D objects into graphics engines for improvisation and modification. This inverse rendering pipeline converts 2D images into editable 3D triangle mesh models within an hour on a single NVIDIA Tensor Core GPU, making them compatible with existing design tools. The technology was showcased using jazz instruments, highlighting its ability to reconstruct objects with accurate materials and lighting for creative workflows in various industries.

title: Nvidia makes big advances in inverse rendering to transform still photos into 3D objects
summary: Nvidia has announced significant progress in "inverse rendering" with its new method, Nvidia 3D MoMa, which uses AI to convert still photos into editable 3D models. This technology allows developers to quickly import objects into graphics engines, modify materials, lighting, and scale, and is expected to benefit industries like gaming, architecture, and design by automating the typically tedious 3D modeling process. The method can reconstruct 3D mesh models, materials, and lighting from images in under an hour, enabling faster creation of virtual and augmented reality applications.

title: Chinese DPU chip firm gains funds, unicorn status ...

The financing round was led by Tencent Holdings Ltd. and included other major investors. Jaguar Microsystems, which employs nearly 400 staff, released an FPGA version of its DPU in 2021 and plans for mass production of its system-chip version by 2023, primarily targeting cloud computing and internet companies, with Tencent expected to be a key customer.

title: Finding NeMo: Sensory Taps NVIDIA AI for Voice and Vision Applications
summary: Sensory, a pioneer in compact AI models for consumer electronics, is leveraging NVIDIA's NeMo toolkit and Triton Inference Server to enhance its voice and vision AI applications. This hybrid computing approach improves features like wake words and speech-to-text accuracy across billions of devices. The collaboration allows for more powerful and adaptable on-device models through cloud connections and over-the-air updates, supporting 17 languages and achieving superior word error rates.

title: These 5 Semiconductor Suppliers Are Undervalued
summary: The article highlights five undervalued semiconductor suppliers—ASML, Teradyne, Applied Materials, Lam Research, and KLA—that offer compelling long-term investment opportunities. Each company boasts a Wide Economic Moat designation from Morningstar, indicating strong competitive advantages and potential for sustained high returns.

title: DDR5: How Faster Memory Speeds Shape The Future
summary: This article discusses the advancements and challenges brought by DDR5 memory, which doubles the data rate of its predecessor, DDR4. It highlights how DDR5's increased speeds and power efficiency enable emerging technologies like IoT and V2X autonomous vehicles. The article also touches upon the future of DDR6, anticipating further speed increases and new signaling innovations to overcome physical limitations.

title: Inferencing made simple with the NetApp DataOps Toolkit
summary: NetApp has introduced new capabilities in its DataOps Toolkit for Kubernetes to simplify the deployment of Triton Inference Server with NetApp persistent storage. This advancement addresses the complexities of AI model inferencing, allowing data scientists and MLOps engineers to deploy Triton Inference Server instances with one simple command, leveraging NetApp's data fabric for seamless synchronization and enterprise-class data protection features like Snapshot copies. The integration aims to streamline the AI lifecycle, particularly for on-premises deployments or those requiring specific storage efficiencies and data sovereignty.

title: Siemens and NVIDIA to Enable Industrial Metaverse
summary: Siemens and NVIDIA announced an expanded partnership to create an industrial metaverse by connecting Siemens Xcelerator and NVIDIA Omniverse platforms. This collaboration aims to transform the manufacturing industry by enabling full-fidelity digital twins and integrating AI systems from edge to cloud. The goal is to accelerate the use of digital twins, improve productivity, and facilitate immersive, physics-based simulations for faster and more confident decision-making across product lifecycles.

title: Building a Silicon Bulwark: How the United States and Taiwan Can Retain Joint Leadership of the Global Semiconductor Industry
summary: This article examines how the United States and Taiwan can jointly maintain their leadership in the global semiconductor industry against challenges, particularly from China's talent poaching. It proposes three key areas for cooperation: strengthening mutual legal assistance, harmonizing export control approaches, and pooling investments in semiconductor R&D and fabrication. The goal is to fortify Taiwan's "silicon shield" into a broader transnational bulwark.

summary: NVIDIA is fostering data center innovation by collaborating with ecosystem partners through its DOCA Software Framework for BlueField DPUs. summary: WNS (Holdings) Limited has acquired Chennai-based enterprise automation services provider Vuram for $165 million. Both companies anticipate enabling clients to accelerate automation, optimization, and transformation of their business models.

summary: Dave Guzzi, General Manager for Systems and Components Partners at Intel, discusses the company's significant commitment to its channel partners, driven by a massive manufacturing investment aimed at shifting chip production away from Asia. He emphasizes the importance of providing partners with secure supply chains and resources like Partner University to help them develop solutions with Intel's emerging technologies, including AI. Guzzi also highlights Intel's ambition to compete in the GPU market, offering partners more choice and leveraging Intel's extensive software development expertise.

title: In a Tough Quarter, Sustainable Strategies Struggled But Stayed Competitive
summary: In the second quarter, sustainable investing strategies faced headwinds as technology stocks, prominent in many ESG portfolios, declined, and energy stocks, often excluded, performed strongly. Despite this, many sustainable equity strategies, particularly those leveraging healthcare and consumer staples, managed to stay competitive and, in some cases, even outperformed the broader market. Over the long term, ESG-focused strategies continue to show strong performance relative to the market, indicating resilience despite short-term market shifts.

title: Teledyne FLIR Introduces Prism AI, Software for the Development of Automotive Thermal Perception Systems
summary: Teledyne FLIR has introduced Prism AI, a software framework designed to help automotive engineers integrate thermal cameras into advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) and autonomous vehicle (AV) systems. Prism AI offers features like visible and thermal image fusion, enhancing detection of pedestrians and animals, especially in low-light conditions. This development aims to improve road safety and assist OEMs in meeting upcoming regulatory requirements for nighttime collision prevention.

title: Nvidia QODA platform integrates quantum, classical computing
summary: Nvidia has launched the Quantum Optimized Device Architecture (QODA) platform, a hybrid environment that merges quantum and classical computing. This platform allows developers to create applications that leverage both systems, optimizing performance for scientific and quantum research and accelerating classical applications for quantum environments. QODA aims to bridge the gap between these two computing paradigms, facilitating quantum applications that utilize existing GPU and AI technologies.

title: NVIDIA Announces Hybrid Quantum-Classical Computing Platform
summary: NVIDIA has introduced QODA (Quantum Optimized Device Architecture), a unified computing platform designed to accelerate quantum research and development across various fields such as AI, HPC, health, and finance. QODA aims to make quantum computing more accessible by providing a coherent hybrid quantum-classical programming model, enabling developers to integrate quantum computing into existing applications. The platform has already garnered collaborations with leading quantum hardware providers, software providers, and supercomputing centers.

title: Nvidia unveils QODA platform to accelerate hybrid quantum-classical computing research
summary: Nvidia has launched its Quantum Optimized Device Architecture (QODA) platform, designed to accelerate hybrid quantum-classical computing research. QODA aims to streamline development by providing a unified environment for supercomputers and quantum processors. This platform allows developers to integrate classical computing resources with quantum hardware from various partners, fostering breakthroughs in areas like chemistry and drug discovery.

title: Red Hat announces Matt Hicks as its new CEO
summary: Red Hat has appointed Matt Hicks as its new president and CEO, succeeding Paul Cormier, who will become the company's chairman. Hicks, a long-time Red Hat employee and key contributor to its OpenShift platform, is expected to continue the company's stable progress and focus on open-source, hybrid cloud solutions. Analysts view Hicks' appointment positively, emphasizing his deep technical knowledge and experience as Red Hat remains a critical revenue driver for IBM.

title: Chip Shortage Turns into Surplus
summary: The global chip shortage, exacerbated by the coronavirus pandemic and high demand for electronics, has unexpectedly turned into a surplus due to high inflation, China's COVID restrictions, and the war in Ukraine, which reduced consumer spending. This shift has severely impacted semiconductor stocks, with companies like Micron Technology reducing production and manufacturers, especially in computing and smartphones, now facing an oversupply. The situation is worsened by hoarding practices, though some sectors like Apple suppliers and, for now, automobile chipmakers, are less affected.

The fund aims to capitalize on the increasing demand for semiconductor chips by focusing on high-growth potential Shariah-compliant companies with strong financials and intellectual property. This fund is the first of its kind in Malaysia, with Nomura Asset Management UK Ltd acting as the investment adviser.

title: How’s That? Startup Ups Game for Cricket, Football and More With Vision AI
summary: TVConal, a deep-tech startup based in Singapore, is leveraging NVIDIA AI and computer vision to develop a sports video analytics platform. This platform automatically flags in-game events and provides performance insights for various sports like cricket, football, tennis, and badminton. By using NVIDIA Metropolis, TAO toolkit, and SDKs, TVConal's solution helps teams, leagues, and broadcasters analyze vast amounts of video data in real time, making sports analysis more efficient and accurate.

title: Pony.ai and SANY Establish Joint Venture to Develop Next Generation of Autonomous Trucks for Mass Production
summary: Pony.ai and SANY Heavy Truck have formed a strategic joint venture to develop and mass-produce next-generation Level 4 autonomous trucks. The collaboration aims to integrate Pony.ai's autonomous driving technology with SANY's heavy truck manufacturing expertise, with small-scale deliveries planned for 2022-2023 and mass production targeting 10,000 units annually by 2024. This partnership is expected to create a sophisticated intelligent logistics ecosystem, enhance road safety, reduce costs, and significantly lower greenhouse gas emissions by focusing on new energy vehicles.

title: Pelosi's husband dumps Nvidia stock as House eyes chip bill
summary: Paul Pelosi, husband of U.S. House Speaker Nancy Pelosi, sold 25,000 shares of Nvidia stock for approximately $4.1 million, days before the House was set to consider a bill providing significant subsidies and tax credits to the U.S. semiconductor industry. This transaction resulted in a loss of over $341,000 for Pelosi, who frequently trades shares in major tech companies. The upcoming legislation aims to boost domestic chip production and competitiveness against China.

title: Samsung warns of weaker chip demand for phones, PCs as people shop less
summary: Samsung Electronics has issued a warning that chip demand from smartphone and PC manufacturers is expected to decline further as consumer spending decreases. This outlook, shared by the world's leading memory chip and smartphone maker, suggests that even the more resilient demand from server clients might see adjustments due to growing recession fears. While Samsung achieved its best April-June operating profit since 2018 driven by strong server chip demand, its mobile business faced profit weakening amidst geopolitical issues, inflation, and rising costs.

title: Pony.ai Express: New Autonomous Trucking Collaboration Powered by NVIDIA DRIVE Orin
summary: Pony.ai and SANY Heavy Truck, China's largest heavy equipment manufacturer, have partnered to develop level 4 autonomous trucks using NVIDIA DRIVE Orin. The collaboration aims to address the rapidly growing package delivery market and driver shortages, with small-scale deliveries starting this year and mass production by 2024. The venture plans to produce approximately 10,000 trucks annually, leveraging NVIDIA DRIVE Orin's high-performance compute capabilities for safe and efficient autonomous operations.

title: Enabling Enterprise Cybersecurity Protection with a DPU-Accelerated, Next-Generation Firewall
summary: NVIDIA and Palo Alto Networks have collaborated to enhance cybersecurity by accelerating VM-Series Next Generation Firewalls (NGFW) using NVIDIA's BlueField Data Processing Unit (DPU). This partnership provides a 5x performance boost and significant CapEx savings by offloading packet inspection from host CPUs to the DPU. The joint solution includes an Intelligent Traffic Offload (ITO) service that optimizes firewall resources, ensuring deep security inspection only for necessary payload flows, thereby improving efficiency and enabling comprehensive zero-trust protection across all hosts.

title: Pony.ai autonomous driving controller built on NVIDIA DRIVE Orin, set for mass production
summary: Pony.ai announced that its Autonomous Driving Controller (ADC), powered by the NVIDIA DRIVE Hyperion compute architecture (DRIVE Orin), has been sampled to customers with plans for mass production starting in Q4 2022. The ADC, featuring NVIDIA DRIVE Orin system-on-chip, offers configurations delivering up to 508 TOPS and is designed for safe, highly advanced intelligent driving across various road conditions. This development marks a significant step towards mass-producing robust autonomous vehicle platforms for both self-driving trucks and robotaxis.

title: Opinion: Which Intel CEO is to blame for the current woes? Or is it actually AMD’s CEO?

The article highlights that Intel's results were so poor that analysts questioned why the company did not pre-announce them.

title: With new federal aid, Minnesota chipmaker expects to speed up expansions
summary: SkyWater Technology, a Minnesota-based semiconductor manufacturer, anticipates accelerating its expansion projects in Minnesota, Indiana, and Florida thanks to the newly approved $52 billion CHIPS Act. While the exact amount of aid SkyWater will receive is unknown, CEO Tom Sonderman believes the funding package will help reduce risks associated with their investments. The CHIPS Act aims to bolster the U.S. chip industry and counter foreign government assistance, primarily from China, by providing direct aid and a 25% tax credit for domestic plant investments.

title: The Take: $52 Billion for Chip Plants… Better Than Nothing
summary: The US House of Representatives passed a $280 billion bill, the Chips and Science Act of 2022, primarily aimed at boosting US semiconductor manufacturing with $52.7 billion in subsidies for new plants. While the legislation is a step towards increasing domestic chip production, SAP global vice president Mike Lackey suggests that this funding might only support about 10 new fabrication facilities, which take years to build. The bill's effectiveness is further questioned by its lack of provisions for crucial capital equipment and the broader supply chain, amidst rapidly growing global demand for semiconductors.

title: Micron 232-Layer TLC NAND in Volume Production
summary: Micron Technology, Inc. has begun volume production of its first 232-layer NAND, which offers the highest areal density, increased capacity, and improved energy efficiency compared to previous generations. This new NAND technology delivers a 50% faster data transfer rate and up to 100% higher write bandwidth, making it suitable for data-intensive applications from client to cloud, including AI, ML, and cloud computing. The 232-layer NAND is produced in Micron's Singapore fab and is initially shipping to customers for component use and in its Crucial SSD consumer product line.

summary: The UCIe™ (Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express™) Consortium has officially incorporated and announced new board members, including Alibaba and NVIDIA, joining founding members like ASE, AMD, Intel, and Samsung. title: Arista Buys Pluribus Networks To Grow Cloud Networking Offering
summary: Arista Networks has acquired Pluribus Networks to enhance its Converged Cloud Fabric offering and strengthen its partnership with Ericsson. This is Arista's second acquisition in the quarter, following Untangle, as it focuses on acquiring technology and talent that align with its culture to expand its cloud networking solutions and address lower-end security and edge threat management markets. The acquisition was disclosed as Arista reported surpassing $1 billion in quarterly revenue for the first time, despite ongoing global supply chain challenges.

title: Pelosi’s Taiwan trip puts the world's biggest chipmaker back in the spotlight of U.S.-China rivalry
summary: Nancy Pelosi's visit to Taiwan brought renewed attention to the island's critical role in the global chip supply chain, specifically highlighting Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC), a key manufacturer for tech giants like Apple and Nvidia. The visit underscored the strategic importance of semiconductors to U.S. national security and its rivalry with China. TSMC's dominance in the foundry market and the ongoing U.S. efforts to boost domestic chip manufacturing and secure supply chains were central themes, with concerns about China's potential actions towards Taiwan posing a significant risk to the global chip market.

title: Expanding the Possibilities
summary: GlobalFoundries (GF) is challenging conventional semiconductor manufacturing by focusing on feature-rich process technology for 70% of the market. The company emphasizes innovation in RF communications, power management, and precision analog, working with industry leaders to deliver solutions across various high-growth markets. GF's efforts, including the GF Connex RF portfolio, GF Fotonix silicon photonics platform, and GF Labs, aim to drive product innovation and accelerate time-to-market.

title: Taiwan dominates the world’s supply of computer chips – no wonder the US is worried
summary: Taiwan holds a dominant position in the global semiconductor market, particularly through TSMC, which controls 53% of the foundry market. This dominance has made Taiwan crucial to US geopolitical and national security interests, especially as semiconductors are vital for advanced technology and military applications. The US is actively working to reduce its reliance on foreign chip manufacturing, encouraging companies like TSMC to establish operations in the US and implementing policies like the Chips and Science Act to boost domestic production.

title: Arista acquires Pluribus Networks for cloud fabric product
summary: Arista Networks has acquired Pluribus Networks to enhance its Unified Cloud Fabric product and gain entry into the telco market. The acquisition will integrate Pluribus's technology to create a software-defined network across various hardware components, targeting 4G/5G telco operators and leveraging relationships with partners like Ericsson and Nvidia. This move follows Arista's strategy of acquiring SDN vendors to bolster its networking capabilities.

title: Turbocharging Multi-Cloud Security and Application Delivery with VirtIO Offloading
summary: This article details how F5 and NVIDIA are addressing inefficiencies in data centers caused by increased virtualization and software-defined architectures by offloading VirtIO to the NVIDIA BlueField-2 DPU. This approach provides optimal acceleration, domain isolation, and dynamic composability, significantly reducing CPU reliance while maintaining flexibility. A demonstration showcased a 320% improvement in throughput and a 66% reduction in processing time when using hardware acceleration with the NVIDIA BlueField-2 DPU compared to running VirtIO on the host.

title: AXS 1.5X PYPL Bull Daily ETF
summary: This article provides a comprehensive overview of the AXS 1.5X PYPL Bull Daily ETF (PYPT), detailing its profile, historical data, and comparisons with alternative ETFs. title: Nvidia Warns of Sales Shortfall as Gaming Revenue Drops
summary: Nvidia Corp. announced a significant sales shortfall for the quarter ending July 31, expecting revenue of $6.7 billion, which is 17% below its May forecast. This reduction is primarily due to a 33% drop in gaming revenue, signaling a potential slowdown in the computer chip market after a pandemic-era boom. The company's stock experienced a decline following this announcement.

title: Nvidia is hit by another ‘crypto hangover,’ and that isn’t the only problem
summary: Nvidia is facing a "crypto hangover" and other issues as the pandemic-era booms in PC sales, videogames, and cryptocurrency decline. The company warned of a $1.4 billion revenue shortfall due to weak gaming equipment sales and excess inventory. Nvidia's stock fell 6.3% on the news, reflecting broader concerns about multiple challenges impacting its core business.

title: Nvidia warns of lower second-quarter revenue on gaming weakness
summary: Nvidia Corp warned of a 19% drop in second-quarter revenue from the prior quarter due to weakness in its gaming business, sending its shares down by about 8%. This follows similar warnings from other chipmakers and is attributed to consumers weighing purchases of discretionary items amidst economic concerns, as well as continued supply chain issues. The company expects to report overall Q2 revenue of approximately $6.70 billion, significantly below analyst estimates.

title: Wall Street closes little changed on Fed policy fears
summary: Wall Street closed mostly flat due to concerns over the Federal Reserve's aggressive stance on inflation following strong jobs data, compounded by a revenue warning from chipmaker Nvidia. Investors are now awaiting consumer price data to assess the Fed's future monetary policy. Despite a recent market rebound, analysts suggest the market might be subject to further pullbacks.

title: JPMorgan Active Growth ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:JGRO) $JGRO
summary: The JPMorgan Active Growth ETF (JGRO) is an actively managed exchange-traded fund that invests in U.S. large-cap companies with strong earnings growth potential. Launched on August 8, 2022, the ETF has $8.27 billion in assets under management and a net expense ratio of 0.44%. title: Cathie Wood sells Block shares to double down on Nvidia
summary: Ark Invest, led by Cathie Wood, sold over $20 million worth of Block (SQ) shares and simultaneously purchased over $65 million worth of Nvidia (NVDA) shares across three of its funds. This move follows Ark's previous decision to exit PayPal (PYPL) to bet on Block, and comes amidst macroeconomic turbulence causing significant losses in various asset classes, including Block and Bitcoin. Ark also recently sold Coinbase (COIN) shares due to regulatory uncertainty.

title: NVIDIA Announces Major Release of Omniverse With New USD Connectors and Tools, Simulation Technologies and Developer Frameworks
summary: NVIDIA has announced a major update to its Omniverse platform, introducing new developer frameworks, tools, apps, and plugins designed to build and connect metaverse worlds. These enhancements include AI-powered tools like Omniverse Avatar Cloud Engine, DeepSearch, and NeuralVDB, along with 11 new USD Connectors to integrate with leading 3D applications and CAD software. The updates aim to simplify virtual world creation and foster collaboration across industries, bridging the physical and virtual realms.

title: NVIDIA and Partners Build Out Universal Scene Description to Accelerate Industrial Metaverse and Next Wave of AI
summary: NVIDIA, in collaboration with Pixar, Adobe, Autodesk, Siemens, and other industry leaders, is launching a multi-year initiative to expand Universal Scene Description (USD) as a foundational language for the open metaverse and 3D internet. The effort aims to extend USD's capabilities beyond visual effects to support industrial applications like architecture, engineering, manufacturing, robotics, and digital twins, introducing features such as international character support, geospatial coordinates, and real-time IoT data streaming. NVIDIA is also providing open-source resources, a compatibility testing suite, and developing USD plugins for popular 3D software to accelerate its adoption across various industries.

title: Nasdaq closes lower as chipmaker Micron's warning renews tech rout
summary: The Nasdaq closed lower on Tuesday following a grim forecast from Micron Technology, which dragged down chip makers and tech stocks. Investors are now anticipating critical U.S. inflation data, which could influence the Federal Reserve's future interest rate decisions to curb inflation. High inflationary figures, especially after a strong jobs report last week, would likely halt any near-term easing of rate hikes and potentially stop the market's recent rally.

title: Chipmakers tumble on fears of worst downturn in 10 years
summary: Semiconductor stocks experienced a significant downturn following Micron Technology Inc.'s warning of slowing demand, raising concerns about the industry heading into a prolonged slump. Analysts believe the sector is entering its worst downturn in a decade, affecting every company and end market. Despite recent shortages and investments, the rapid evaporation of demand has taken experts by surprise, with some companies like Micron already cutting future spending.

title: AMD Stock Is a Bargain
summary: Morningstar considers AMD stock a bargain with a fair value estimate of $130 per share, giving it a 4-star rating and a narrow economic moat. The company is praised for its impressive growth, market share gains against Intel, and strong execution in new chip designs, especially in the data center and PC markets. However, high uncertainty remains due to the cyclical semiconductor industry and AMD's smaller scale compared to Intel and Nvidia.

summary: The article discusses how semiconductor technology drives many thematic investment indexes, particularly after the increased recognition of their importance due to pandemic-related supply issues. It highlights the impact of the newly signed CHIPS and Science Act, which provides significant subsidies to boost domestic chip manufacturing. The piece also explains how various thematic indexes, such as those for electric vehicles, streaming, gaming, and even space technology, are directly or indirectly exposed to the semiconductor industry and stand to benefit from these developments.

title: Thematic Times: Semiconductors Power Thematic Indexes
summary: The article discusses how semiconductor stocks are crucial to many thematic indexes, particularly after the CHIPS and Science Act. It highlights direct and indirect exposure of various thematic indexes to semiconductors and the long-term benefits of the CHIPS Act for the industry and end users. The growth of the semiconductor market is primarily driven by the automotive sector, data storage, and wireless communications.

title: Desktop CPU Sales Lowest in 30 Years, AMD Gains Market Share Anyway (Updated)
summary: Desktop CPU shipments hit a nearly 30-year low in Q2 2022, marking the largest year-over-year decline in Mercury Research's records. Despite the overall market slump, AMD significantly increased its market share and revenue in desktop, mobile, and server segments, setting new records for x86 processor share and mobile unit share. Intel, in contrast, reported a rare loss and delayed key products, indicating a challenging period for the long-standing leader.

title: Smart Devices, Smart Manufacturing: Pegatron Taps AI, Digital Twins
summary: Pegatron, a major manufacturer of tech devices, is integrating AI and digital twin technology to enhance its manufacturing processes. The company built an AI platform, Cambrian, using NVIDIA technologies to significantly improve product inspection, reducing defects and improving efficiency. Pegatron is now piloting NVIDIA Omniverse for developing digital twins of inspection machines and envisions creating a full virtual factory to further streamline operations and predict potential issues.

title: A message to prospectors of the semiconductor gold rush
summary: Governments worldwide are heavily investing in semiconductor manufacturing, recognizing their critical role in future technologies like AI, IoT, and 5G/6G, and their impact on national security and economic growth. While India is making efforts with a significant budgetary allocation, the article argues for a more strategic approach, focusing on building a comprehensive semiconductor ecosystem starting with simpler devices, rather than just pouring money into the industry, to avoid past mistakes observed in China and the USSR. The author emphasizes the long-term commitment needed for India to become a semiconductor superpower.

title: Lam Research to open its second R&D centre in India
summary: US-based semiconductor equipment supplier Lam Research is establishing its second R&D center in India in September, aiming to enable local design completion and reduce reliance on its US counterparts. The new facility will feature an advanced hardware engineering lab for deposition, etching, and wet processing, alongside AR/VR capabilities. This expansion underscores India's growing importance in the semiconductor design ecosystem, despite the manufacturing sector being in its early stages.

title: Startup Digs Into Public Filings With GPU-Driven Machine Learning to Serve Up Alternative Financial Data Services
summary: Intrinio, a startup based in St. Petersburg, Fla., uses GPU-driven machine learning to parse publicly available financial data, offering an alternative to traditional, bundled financial data products. Co-founded by Rachel Carpenter and Joseph French, Intrinio provides à la carte subscription services for equities, options, estimates, ETFs, and ESG data, making it more affordable and accessible for fintech innovators and startups. The company's technology significantly reduces errors and streamlines data cleansing and standardization, allowing clients like Robinhood, FTX, and Aiera to integrate high-quality financial data into their platforms.

title: Startup’s Vision AI Software Trains Itself — in One Hour — to Detect Manufacturing Defects in Real Time
summary: Covision Quality, an NVIDIA Metropolis member, has developed AI-based visual inspection software that can train itself in one hour to detect manufacturing defects. This software, accelerated by NVIDIA RTX A5000 GPUs, significantly reduces false-negative rates by up to 90% and pseudo-scrap rates, improving efficiency and sustainability in industrial production. Covision's solution allows for real-time defect detection without extensive coding or image labeling, addressing a major challenge in automated visual inspection scaling.

title: Report: Qualcomm plans to return to the server chip market
summary: Qualcomm Inc. is reportedly planning to re-enter the server chip market four years after exiting it, seeking customers for a new server processor. This new processor is based on technology acquired from Nuvia Inc. for $1.4 billion and is being evaluated by Amazon Web Services Inc. The move aligns with Qualcomm's strategy to expand beyond mobile and boost revenue, potentially increasing competition for Intel Corp. and Advanced Micro Devices Inc.

title: Intel shares new details about upcoming Meteor Lake processor series
summary: Intel has revealed new technical details about its upcoming Meteor Lake processor series, which will utilize chiplet technology for desktop and laptop CPUs. These processors will feature five chiplets, with the primary CPU module manufactured by Intel and other vital components like the GPU and I/O module produced by TSMC. This chiplet architecture allows for greater flexibility in design, improved manufacturing efficiency, and better performance through 3D stacking with Intel's Foveros technology.

title: Making AI Run At Any Scale But Not At All Costs
summary: This article discusses the challenges and solutions for scaling AI applications, highlighting how companies like HPE and Lenovo are developing accessible AI products. It focuses on Anyscale, a company founded by UC Berkeley researchers, which commercializes the open-source Ray framework to simplify distributed AI computing and make it easier for enterprises to develop and deploy AI models without extensive infrastructure expertise.

title: Nvidia sales forecast falls about $1 billion short of expectations, stock falls
summary: Nvidia's sales forecast for the current quarter fell approximately $1 billion short of analyst expectations, leading to a drop in its stock. The company confirmed a sharp reduction in profit and is working through inventory before releasing its new chip architecture. For the fiscal third quarter, Nvidia predicted revenue between $5.78 billion to $6.02 billion, while analysts had projected $6.91 billion.

title: Corsair Reveals Bendable OLED Ultrawide Gaming Monitor
summary: Corsair has introduced the Xeneon Flex 45WQHD240 OLED, a 45-inch ultrawide gaming monitor featuring a bendable OLED panel from LG. This monitor offers user-adjustable curvature up to 800R, or it can remain perfectly flat for productivity. It boasts impressive specs including a 0.03ms response time, 240Hz refresh rate, and 1000 nits peak brightness, making it suitable for immersive gaming and HDR content.

title: Fintech Company Blocks Fraud Attacks for Financial Institutions With AI and NVIDIA GPUs
summary: Featurespace, an NVIDIA Inception member, leverages AI and NVIDIA GPUs to combat financial crime like credit-card fraud and money laundering. Their ARIC Risk Hub platform uses deep learning models trained on NVIDIA GPUs to detect fraudulent transactions in real-time, building complex behavioral profiles of genuine customers. This technology has helped 70 financial institutions detect fraud faster, reducing losses and protecting over 500 million consumers.

title: Why Supermicro for On-Prem Data Centers
summary: Supermicro offers compelling advantages for on-premise data centers, enabling organizations to deploy the latest CPU and GPU technologies quickly due to Supermicro's close relationships with suppliers. The company provides a broad range of application and workload-optimized server and storage configurations, including liquid cooling options, to meet specific performance requirements and reduce TCO. Supermicro also offers comprehensive IT solutions, from single nodes to large clusters, with full assembly, testing, and rack integration services to ensure optimal performance and customer satisfaction.

title: AMD Set To Become TSMC’s Second Largest 5nm Customer Courtesy Of Ryzen 7000
summary: AMD is projected to become TSMC's second-largest customer for 5nm technology, primarily driven by its upcoming Ryzen 7000 series processors. These new CPUs, including desktop, notebook, and datacenter variants, will extensively utilize TSMC's 5nm process node. This increased demand will solidify AMD's position as a major client for the Taiwanese chip manufacturer, second only to Apple.
