summary: Nvidia recently revealed new details about its "Grace" Arm server CPU at the Hot Chips 34 conference, confirming it will use Armv9 specification cores and SVE2 vector math units. The article explores the potential design, core count, and the decision to use LPDDR5 memory, highlighting Grace's integration into Grace-Grace or Grace-Hopper superchip complexes and its performance estimates for memory-intensive AI workloads like GPT-3.

title: AMD launching what it claims is ‘fastest processer in the world for gaming’ in September
summary: AMD announced the launch of its new Ryzen 7000 series gaming processors, touted as the "fastest processor in the world for gaming" by CEO Lisa Su. The processors are based on a 5-nanometer Zen 4 core architecture. This release comes amidst a challenging period for PC sales, with the low-end Ryzen 5 7600x model priced at $299.

title: Gaming industry advancing development of virtual ecosystem: Co-Founder of Roundhill Ball Metaverse ETF
summary: Matthew Ball, CEO and Co-Founder of the Roundhill Ball Metaverse ETF, discusses the progress of the gaming industry in developing a virtual ecosystem. The discussion covers the future of virtual real estate companies, the capabilities of 3D rendering, and the practical aspects of building a virtual world.

title: U.S. Restricts Sales of Sophisticated Chips to China and Russia
summary: The Biden administration has imposed new restrictions on the sale of sophisticated computer chips, specifically high-end graphics processing units (GPUs), to China and Russia. This move, affecting companies like Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices, aims to prevent These chips, crucial for supercomputers and artificial intelligence used in applications like weapons development and intelligence gathering, from being used for military purposes. Nvidia estimates this restriction will impact approximately $400 million in revenue.

title: Nvidia Warns of Sales Hit From New U.S. Chip Licensing Requirements for China
summary: Nvidia Corp. announced that new U.S. licensing requirements for shipping advanced chips to China could result in a loss of up to $400 million in quarterly sales. The company was notified on Friday that it would need a license from the U.S. government for certain cutting-edge chip sales to China and Russia. This development follows President Biden's recent signing of the Chips and Science Act of 2022.

title: Nvidia’s Red Scare, Costco’s Going “There” & No Campbell’s Soup For You!
summary: Nvidia experienced a significant stock drop after the U.S. Commerce Department restricted the sale of its AI-related chips to China and Russia, citing national security concerns, which is expected to cost the company $400 million quarterly. Meanwhile, Costco is rumored to be considering a membership fee increase following a similar move by Sam's Club, and Campbell's reported earnings highlighted the impact of inflation on food production costs. The article also touches on Micron's investment in a new chipmaking plant and Signet Jewelers' mixed quarterly results amidst inflation fears.

title: Nvidia says U.S. government allows A.I. chip development in China
summary: Nvidia confirmed that the U.S. government has permitted it to continue developing its H100 artificial intelligence chip in China, despite new export restrictions on high-performance AI chips to the region. The restrictions, which still ban sales of the A100 and H100 chips to China and Russia, are expected to cost Nvidia $400 million in revenue for the current quarter. Developing the H100 in China is allowed, and Nvidia can ship existing AI chips from Hong Kong until September 2023.

title: U.S. officials order Nvidia to halt sales of top AI chips to China
summary: U.S. officials have ordered Nvidia to cease exporting its top AI chips, the A100 and H100, to China, significantly escalating the U.S. crackdown on China's technological advancements. This move, aimed at preventing the chips from being used for military purposes, could hinder Chinese firms' ability to perform advanced AI work and impact Nvidia's future sales in the region. Rival AMD also received similar restrictions on its MI250 chips, but stated the impact on its business would not be material.

title: ARM is suing Qualcomm for licensing and trademark violations
summary: ARM is suing Qualcomm for breach of contract and trademark infringement over Qualcomm's acquisition of chip startup Nuvia Inc. ARM claims Nuvia's licenses, which are critical for chip design, cannot be transferred to Qualcomm without permission and were terminated after negotiations failed. The lawsuit threatens Qualcomm's strategy to expand into the laptop and server processor markets, and highlights a growing conflict between two major players in the chip industry.

title: New U.S. curbs on sales of Nvidia AI chips to China spark selloff
summary: New U.S. restrictions on exports of advanced AI chips from Nvidia and AMD to China have caused Nvidia's stock to fall over 11%. The curbs, aimed at limiting China's technological prowess, specifically target Nvidia's H100 and A100 chips which are crucial for AI and machine learning applications. While potentially impacting Nvidia's business in China, the U.S. government has made some allowances for the completion and support of the H100 chip.

title: Nvidia could take a $400M revenue hit from new government restrictions on AI chips
summary: New government restrictions on the sale of AI chips to China could cost Nvidia an estimated $400 million in revenue. Both Nvidia and AMD are facing these limitations on their ability to sell advanced data center chips in the Chinese market.

title: Nvidia Halting Chip Production to China, Fiber in Hawaii, Broadband Data Deadline Today
summary: The US government has instructed Nvidia to stop exporting two advanced computing chips to China, citing concerns over potential military use and impact on China's AI advancements. Meanwhile, Hawaiian Telecom is expanding its fiber internet service to nearly 10,000 homes and businesses on Kaua'i and participating in the Affordable Connectivity Program. Additionally, Thursday marks the deadline for providers to submit their broadband availability data for FCC maps as part of the Broadband Data Collection.

title: Taiwan chip magnate pledges cash for defense against China: 'I'm telling everyone to oppose the CCP'
summary: Robert Tsao, founder of Taiwan's first semiconductor company UMC, has pledged $32 million of his personal wealth to fund the Kuma Academy, which trains Taiwan's civilian defense corps. This initiative aims to train over three million "civilian warriors" and sharpshooters annually to defend against a potential Chinese invasion. Tsao, who has regained Taiwanese citizenship after giving it up, stated his strong opposition to the Chinese Communist Party, a stance he adopted after witnessing the crackdown on pro-democracy supporters in Hong Kong.

title: Texas Instruments Inc. stock outperforms competitors despite losses on the day
summary: Shares of Texas Instruments Inc. (TXN) fell 1.90% to $163.00 on Friday, despite an overall dismal trading session for the stock market where the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average also declined. The stock closed $39.26 shy of its 52-week high, but still outperformed some competitors like NVIDIA Corp., Intel Corp., and Qualcomm Inc., which experienced larger percentage drops. Trading volume for Texas Instruments Inc. was below its 50-day average.

title: Major stock averages slide for third week, Nasdaq posts six-day losing streak
summary: U.S. equities concluded their third consecutive weekly decline, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500, and Nasdaq Composite all falling. The Nasdaq recorded its first six-day losing streak since 2019. Despite a solid August jobs report, fears persist that the Federal Reserve will continue aggressive interest rate hikes to combat inflation, leading to market nervousness and concerns about retesting June lows.

summary: This article identifies seven growth stocks that have the potential to appreciate tenfold by 2027, despite some experiencing declines in 2022. title: Game on: Why esports and gaming could take it to the next level
summary: The esports and gaming sector, a multi-billion-dollar industry, continues to grow despite recent slowdowns attributed to supply chain delays and shifting consumer choices post-pandemic. Analysts and industry experts are confident in long-term growth, citing upcoming title launches and easing parts shortages. Mobile gaming remains the primary driver of revenue growth globally, while esports is gaining mainstream traction with significant investment and increasing popularity in emerging markets.

title: Chip Delivery Times Shrink in August
summary: Global chip delivery times shortened in August to an average of 26.8 weeks, a slight improvement signifying easing supply shortages due to slowing demand for products like phones and PCs. Despite this, certain semiconductors such as power management and microcontrollers remain hard to acquire, and the industry struggles to match supply with demand, leading to concerns about over-ordering and inventory build-up. The Philadelphia Stock Market Semiconductor Index has seen a significant downturn, reflecting investor apprehension.

summary: The Biden administration plans to expand restrictions on U.S. semiconductor and chipmaking tool exports to China, targeting advanced AI chips and manufacturing equipment. These new regulations will codify earlier limitations imposed on companies like KLA Corp, Lam Research Corp, Applied Materials Inc, Nvidia Corp, and Advanced Micro Devices. The move is part of the U.S. strategy to curb China's technological advancements and strengthen its domestic semiconductor industry through initiatives like the $50 billion CHIPS Act.

title: Can the West wean itself off Taiwan’s semiconductors?
summary: The article discusses the West's reliance on Taiwan, particularly Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), for semiconductors and the efforts by the US and EU to onshore chip production due to geopolitical tensions with China. Despite significant investments like the US Chips Act and the European Chips Act, experts believe completely weaning off Taiwanese semiconductors would be costly and time-consuming, possibly creating new supply chain problems. The piece also highlights the complex nature of the global semiconductor supply chain, as US-made chips have been found in Russian weaponry despite sanctions.

summary: Supermicro has launched a new 8U Universal GPU server designed for large-scale AI training, NVIDIA Omniverse, and the Metaverse. This server features eight NVIDIA H100 Tensor Core GPUs, offering maximum performance and flexibility. Its advanced airflow design helps reduce Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) in data centers while maintaining high performance.

title: MicroVision's Lidar Solution Supported on NVIDIA DRIVE Autonomous Vehicle Platform
summary: MicroVision announced that its MAVIN DR lidar system is now supported on the NVIDIA DRIVE AGX platform, enabling true highway-pilot functionality for OEMs. This integration aims to accelerate the adoption of advanced safety features in vehicles by providing high-resolution sensor technology with low latency. The MAVIN DR system is also supported on the NVIDIA DRIVE Sim simulation platform for development and validation.

title: Tech stocks crushed in market selloff
summary: The six largest U.S. tech companies collectively lost over $500 billion in value following an unexpectedly high August inflation report. The Nasdaq Composite experienced its steepest drop since June 2020, sinking 5.16%. Major companies like Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, and Nvidia saw significant declines, with the report potentially influencing further aggressive interest rate hikes from the Fed.

title: Company created by two South Africans tops S&P 500 30-year performance
summary: Monster Beverage Corporation, co-founded by two South African WITS graduates, has ranked as the top-performing stock in the S&P 500 over the last 30 years, achieving a staggering 213,088% total return. The company, initially Hansen Natural Corporation, was acquired in 1990 by Rodney Sacks and Hilton Schlosberg and saw significant growth after launching Monster Energy in 2002. This success story highlights the remarkable financial performance of the energy drink giant, even outperforming tech titans like Amazon, Apple, and Nvidia.

title: Supermicro Announces 8U H100 HGX Server
summary: Supermicro has announced its new 8U Universal GPU Server, incorporating eight NVIDIA H100 Tensor Core GPUs, designed for large-scale AI training, NVIDIA Omniverse, and Metaverse applications. This server increases AI performance with improved thermal density, enabling lower power consumption and operation at higher data center temperatures, while supporting both current and next-generation CPUs and GPUs. The company is expanding its leading GPU server lineup with this addition, offering flexibility with front and rear I/O, AC or DC power support, and liquid cooling options.

title: Arm unveils updated Neoverse CPU roadmap, targeting cloud, hyperscale and HPC workloads
summary: Arm has announced an updated Neoverse CPU roadmap to provide a foundation for various workloads in cloud, hyperscale, and high-performance computing. The new Neoverse V2, codenamed Demeter, aims to deliver top per-thread performance and power efficiency, with partners like Nvidia already integrating it. Additionally, Arm detailed upcoming N-series and E-series chip designs set for a 2023 launch, catering to different compute needs prioritizing thread count or data plane processing.

summary: This article explores the futuristic concept of space-based data centers, following the current trend of underwater data centers. title: Why Liz Truss is desperate for a Cambridge chipmaker to list in London
summary: British Prime Minister Liz Truss and Chancellor Kwasi Kwarteng are making a final attempt to persuade Cambridge-based chipmaker Arm Holdings to list on the London Stock Exchange. Arm, currently owned by Japanese conglomerate SoftBank, had previously indicated a preference for listing in New York, posing a significant challenge for London's markets which have struggled to attract IPOs. summary: NVIDIA has introduced DLSS 3, an AI-powered performance multiplier that leverages neural rendering to significantly boost frame rates by up to 4x compared to brute-force rendering, while maintaining image quality. summary: NVIDIA announced DRIVE Thor, its next-generation centralized computer for autonomous vehicles, delivering up to 2,000 teraflops of performance. summary: Columbia Threadneedle Investments announced the three-year anniversary of its Columbia Research Enhanced Core ETF (RECS) and Columbia Research Enhanced Value ETF (REVS). These strategic beta ETFs, launched in 2019, leverage quantitative investment research and active insights, offering a cost-effective and tax-efficient vehicle for passive benchmark investors. Both funds have shown strong performance, with RECS achieving a 5-star Overall Morningstar Rating and REVS a 3-star rating, affirming their objective of enhancing market exposure within passive investments.

title: Kroger, Albertsons spin-off is extra ammunition in regulatory battle
summary: Kroger and Albertsons are proposing to divest up to 650 stores, potentially through a spin-off to Albertsons shareholders, to gain regulatory approval for their $24.6 billion merger. This unusual structure aims to expedite divestitures amidst regulatory scrutiny and challenges in finding buyers for unionized stores, especially after a previous failed divestiture involving Albertsons and Safeway. The FTC, under Chair Lina Khan, is expected to closely examine the proposal given her skepticism towards large mergers impacting consumers.

title: U.S. Speaker Pelosi's husband sold Nvidia, Micron options at a loss
summary: U.S. House Speaker Nancy Pelosi's husband, Paul Pelosi, sold call options in chipmakers Micron Technology and Nvidia, incurring losses close to $1 million. The transactions were disclosed in a transparency filing, which also showed he exercised call options for Alphabet shares and allowed Walt Disney call options to expire at a loss. This comes amid scrutiny over stock trading by lawmakers and their families, leading to legislative efforts to restrict such activities.

title: The Sweeping Impact of New U.S. Semiconductor Restrictions
summary: New U.S. restrictions on semiconductor sales, chipmaking equipment, and supercomputer parts are significantly impacting China's chip industry, causing a potential brain drain as American personnel face tough choices. While these policies aim to curb China's technological ambitions, they are also a "double-edged sword" for U.S. companies that rely on the Chinese market. Experts suggest these measures could accelerate China's push for self-sufficiency in semiconductors and shift focus towards mature chip technologies.

title: Credo Announces 1.6Tbps OSFP-XD HiWire AECs Targeting Hyperscaler Spine Switching
summary: Credo Technology Group Holding Ltd announced its new 1.6Tb OSFP-XD HiWire CLOS Active Electrical Cable (AEC), designed for hyperscale data centers requiring high-density spine switching. This AEC supports speeds up to 1.6Tbps, cable lengths up to 2.75m, and consumes less than 20W of power, making it energy-efficient and suitable for next-generation 51.2Tbps switches in a 1U form factor. The product leverages a 12nm process for cost-effectiveness and is being showcased at the OCP Summit.

title: Gartner Top 10 Tech Trends For 2023: Metaverse, AI, Cloud
summary: Gartner has released its top 10 technology trends for 2023, focusing on themes like optimizing resilience, scaling solutions, and pioneering new opportunities amidst economic uncertainty. The trends include the metaverse, super apps, adaptive AI, industry cloud platforms, and sustainability, emphasizing technology's role in addressing global challenges and driving business value beyond just cost savings. Each trend is accompanied by an example of its real-world application.

title: Samsung, Qualcomm unveil industry’s fastest LPDDR5X DRAM chip
summary: Samsung Electronics Co. has successfully demonstrated the performance of its LPDDR5X DRAM on Qualcomm’s Snapdragon mobile platform, achieving an industry-leading speed of 8.5 gigabits per second (Gbps). This advancement surpasses Samsung's previous record and solidifies its leadership in the memory market. The new high-speed, low-power memory is expected to enhance mobile, gaming, camera, and AI applications and find broader use in PCs, HPC, servers, and autonomous driving.

title: Supermicro Extends Best of Breed Server Building Block Solutions to Include a Broad Set of OCP Technologies - Driving Customer Innovation and Time-to-Market
summary: Supermicro is expanding its server portfolio to incorporate open hardware and open-source technologies, aiming to drive innovation and reduce proprietary lock-in for customers. These solutions, including an 8U 8-GPU AI training system and OCP 3.0 compliant AIOM cards, integrate best-in-class components like Intel, AMD, and ARM CPUs and NVIDIA GPUs, alongside open technologies such as OpenBMC and Open BIOS. This initiative provides customers with high-performance, efficient, and flexible server options for various applications, from cloud and AI/ML to storage and 5G/Edge computing.

title: Adobe Advances 3D, Immersive and Metaverse Experiences With New Products
summary: Adobe announced significant advancements in its Substance 3D tools, introducing new products like 3D Capture and Substance 3D Modeler to facilitate the creation of 3D and metaverse-ready immersive experiences. The company also revealed a partnership with Meta to integrate Substance 3D tools into the Quest platform, making 3D content creation more accessible. These innovations aim to support creators and brands in transitioning into new mediums, emphasizing ease of use and sustainability with a new Substance 3D Sustainability Calculator.

title: Oracle Cloud adding tens of thousands of Nvidia chips for AI
summary: Oracle Corp and Nvidia Corp are expanding their partnership, with Oracle Cloud adding tens of thousands of Nvidia's A100 and H100 GPUs to boost AI-related computational work. This expansion addresses the growing demand for AI infrastructure as AI models become more complex. Nvidia currently dominates the accelerator chip market for AI, holding an 85% share among the six largest cloud providers.

title: Oracle and NVIDIA Partner to Speed AI Adoption for Enterprises
summary: Oracle and NVIDIA have expanded their long-standing alliance through a multi-year partnership aimed at accelerating AI adoption for enterprises. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) will significantly increase its GPU capacity with NVIDIA's A100 and upcoming H100 GPUs, supporting the full stack of NVIDIA AI software and services. This collaboration will provide enterprises with a broad, accessible portfolio for AI training and deep learning inference, integrating NVIDIA AI platforms into OCI to drive innovation across various industries.

title: US chip war with China creates 'serious challenges' for industry, says TSMC, but 'not us' says ASML
summary: The US chip war with China is creating "serious challenges" for the semiconductor industry, according to TSMC, due to new US restrictions on supplying Chinese tech companies with advanced chipmaking equipment. However, ASML Holding NV, a European chip equipment manufacturer, claims it will not be significantly impacted by these restrictions. ASML's CEO stated that the US rules do not amend regulations for lithography equipment shipped from the Netherlands, and the company expects limited direct impact on its 2023 shipment plan, with demand for its machines remaining strong.

title: Oracle Cloud adds NVIDIA chips, software to speed enterprise AI uptake
summary: Oracle has expanded its partnership with NVIDIA to integrate tens of thousands of NVIDIA's AI-processing graphics chips and software tools into Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI). This aims to accelerate enterprise AI adoption across industries like banking, healthcare, and manufacturing by offering powerful A100 and upcoming H100 GPUs. The collaboration will also provide access to NVIDIA software like RAPIDS Accelerator and Clara for enhanced AI performance, medical imaging, and drug discovery.

title: Why Are Semiconductor Stocks Getting Crushed?
summary: Semiconductor stocks have experienced significant losses in 2022 due to growing recession fears, oversupply from pandemic-driven demand, and new strict U.S. export restrictions on sales to China. These restrictions, particularly impacting high-performance chips and manufacturing equipment, are expected to cost several firms hundreds of millions to billions in revenue. While the near-term outlook is dim, the long-term growth expectation for the semiconductor market remains intact, despite anticipated cyclical downturns.

title: US weighs China tech restrictions on quantum computing and AI
summary: The Biden administration is considering new export controls to limit China's access to emerging computing technologies like quantum computing and artificial intelligence. These potential restrictions follow earlier measures aimed at curbing China's use of advanced semiconductors for military and surveillance purposes. The move risks further escalating tensions with China and forcing other nations to choose between the two economic powers.

title: 7 Virtual Reality Stocks to Buy to Bet on the Coming VR Boom
summary: The virtual reality market is projected to grow significantly to over $227 billion by 2029, presenting a massive opportunity for investors, especially as many top VR stocks are currently oversold. This article highlights seven virtual reality stocks to consider, including the ProShares Metaverse ETF (VERS) for diversification, Roblox (RBLX) as a leading social metaverse platform, and tech giants like Microsoft (MSFT) and Apple (AAPL) that are heavily investing in VR/AR. Other recommendations include Nvidia (NVDA) for its Omniverse platform, Matterport (MTTR) for its exposure to "digital twins," and Unity Software (U) which recently received a "buy" rating.

title: 2020s–Today
summary: The article details SLB's (formerly Schlumberger) strategic evolution from the 2020s to today, focusing on its commitment to decarbonization and a balanced planet. It outlines the company's shift towards new energy ventures like geothermal, clean hydrogen, and lithium while continuing to innovate in oil and gas with digital solutions and emissions reduction technologies. Key events include brand changes, major collaborations, and advancements in AI, energy storage, and sustainability, emphasizing SLB's net-zero emissions goal by 2050 and its push for diversity.

title: China’s Biren GPUs Can’t Be Made at TSMC Due To US Regulations & Competition With NVIDIA
summary: Birentech, a Chinese chip startup, is reportedly barred from manufacturing its Biren GPUs at TSMC due to US regulations aimed at restricting China's access to advanced AI and datacenter chips. This decision is influenced by the Biren BR100's potential to outperform NVIDIA's A100 chips, which are already banned for the Chinese market, and could severely impact Birentech's manufacturing plans.

title: Rambus Announces PCIe 6.0: Powering Next-Gen High-Performance Data Center & AI Solutions
summary: Rambus has unveiled its new PCIe 6.0 interface subsystem, an advanced solution designed for the next generation of data centers and AI applications. This subsystem, comprising PHY and controller IP, delivers data rates up to 64 GT/s and supports the latest CXL 3.0 specification for enhanced memory sharing and pooling. It features an Integrity and Data Encryption (IDE) engine for data protection and is backward compatible with previous PCIe generations.

title: Rambus announces next-gen PCIe 6.0 interface for data centers, AI systems
summary: Rambus has unveiled its next-generation PCIe 6.0 Interface Subsystem, designed for high-performance data centers and AI SoCs, offering speeds up to 64 GT/s. This subsystem includes PHY and controller IP, supports CXL 3.0, and is optimized for advanced heterogeneous computing architectures with features like an Integrity and Data Encryption engine. It ensures compatibility with previous PCIe generations while introducing innovations like low-latency Forward Error Correction.

title: Chips and China
summary: This article examines the implications of the U.S. chip sanctions on China, contrasting the integrated model of Intel with the modular approach of TSMC to explain the complexities of semiconductor manufacturing. It analyzes the long and difficult path China faces to build a self-sufficient advanced chip industry, discussing its unique advantages and the potential geopolitical consequences, particularly for Taiwan. The author concludes by raising concerns about the immediate effects of the sanctions and the potential for mutually assured economic destruction.

title: Lotus Eletre to debut ECARX's next-generation digital head unit
summary: ECARX's next-generation digital head unit (DHU) will debut on the new Lotus Eletre Hyper-SUV, featuring a dual-chip system for advanced processing and an immersive multi-screen user experience with customisable displays. The DHU utilizes Qualcomm's Snapdragon 8155 chipset and Unreal Engine for graphic rendering, ensuring a seamless user experience with real-time data from the car's Advanced Driver Assistance System. This collaboration between ECARX and Lotus is set to redefine in-car technology, furthering Lotus' transition into a global performance car business with smart electric vehicles.

title: Why Are Semiconductor Shares Being Crushed?
summary: Semiconductor stocks are facing significant declines in 2022 due to multiple factors, including recession fears, weak PC sales, and strict US export restrictions on sales to China. These restrictions are expected to heavily impact major companies like Nvidia and AMD, although the long-term growth outlook for the overall semiconductor market remains positive, albeit with near-term uncertainties.

title: Mobileye pops more than 37% in market debut after spinning out of Intel
summary: Mobileye, Intel's self-driving car technology company, saw its shares surge over 37% in its stock market debut after spinning out of Intel. The IPO, which valued Mobileye at around $17 billion, raised $861 million, with Intel planning to use some proceeds to build chip factories. This market debut provides a notable tech IPO in a slow year, despite Mobileye's valuation being below Intel's initial expectations.

title: Lowe’s opens tech hub
summary: Lowe's has opened a new 357,000-sq.-ft. tech hub in Charlotte, N.C., centralizing its technology development activities to support its goal of becoming the most customer-centric omnichannel retailer. The facility, designed for innovation and collaboration, will employ up to 2,000 tech professionals and focus on projects like its interactive virtual store models ("digital twins") and the "Measure Your Space" app feature. This move aligns with Lowe's commitment to leveraging emerging technology to evolve its brand and services.

title: Silicon Labs CEO Transforms Company to IoT Chip Designer
summary: Silicon Labs CEO Matt Johnson is transforming the company into a "pure-play" IoT chip designer, focusing solely on wireless connectivity and IoT devices. The company aims to become the undisputed leader in this space, having doubled its revenue in two years and being an early adopter in unifying various IoT standards like Matter, Zigbee, and Zwave. Despite facing competition from larger players and a recent softening of demand, Johnson sees significant growth potential, particularly in areas like digital retail labels and secure hardware.

title: Intel's Mobileye unit valued at $22 bln as shares cruise higher
summary: Mobileye Global Inc., Intel's self-driving technology unit, debuted strongly on the U.S. stock market, reaching a valuation of $21.8 billion despite earlier IPO target reductions. The company's chief communications officer highlighted the importance of gaining a public platform and product visibility, especially for its SuperVision product, amid a challenging year for U.S. IPOs. Mobileye, which was previously listed before its acquisition by Intel in 2017, competes in the fiercely competitive assisted driving market, projecting deployment in 270 million cars by 2030.

title: Qualcomm Inc. stock underperforms Thursday when compared to competitors
summary: Shares of Qualcomm Inc. (QCOM) fell 2.89% on Thursday, closing at $114.70, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose and the S&P 500 Index fell. This marked the stock's second consecutive day of losses and positioned it below its 52-week high. Qualcomm underperformed some competitors like NVIDIA Corp. and Cisco Systems Inc., though it fared slightly better than Alphabet Inc. Class A.

title: AMD Issues Performance Advisory for Ryzen 7000 Processors
summary: AMD has released a performance advisory for its new Ryzen 7000 processors, acknowledging reports of unexpected performance variations in certain games. The company is actively investigating these issues and plans to collaborate with game developers and hardware partners for optimization. AMD also addressed concerns about Windows 11 performance, stating that their testing showed no significant differences compared to Windows 10.

title: Arm Could Change Licensing Model to Charge OEMs Directly
summary: Arm might change its licensing model by requiring OEMs to license almost all of its IP if they wish to use its CPU IP, directly challenging existing deals and potentially pushing chipmakers toward alternatives like RISC-V. This potential shift, revealed through Qualcomm's counterclaim in a legal dispute, would prevent mixing Arm's IP with other companies' designs (e.g., AMD GPUs in Samsung chips). The change is expected to take effect in 2025, with exemptions for long-term licensees like NVIDIA and Apple.

title: Granite Ridge Resources (GRNT) Stock Price, News & Analysis $GRNT
summary: This article provides a comprehensive analysis of Granite Ridge Resources (GRNT) stock, including its current price, news, and various financial metrics. It covers analyst ratings, earnings forecasts, dividend strength, short interest, and insider trading activity. The company operates as a non-operated oil and gas exploration and production entity, holding a portfolio of wells in the Permian and other US basins.

title: At NetApp INSIGHT 2022, Dive Into NVIDIA DGX BasePOD and NetApp ONTAP AI
summary: This article announces NVIDIA's participation as a sponsor at NetApp INSIGHT 2022, highlighting solutions for operationalizing AI use cases. It introduces NVIDIA DGX BasePOD as a foundation for AI infrastructure, including NetApp ONTAP AI, and discusses how these solutions help businesses deploy proven models faster. The piece also outlines NVIDIA DGX-Ready Managed Services for managing AI infrastructure and filling IT skills gaps.

title: Micron Ships World's Most Advanced DRAM Technology With 1-Beta Node
summary: Micron Technology has announced it is shipping qualification samples of its 1β (1-beta) DRAM technology to select smartphone manufacturers and chipset partners, achieving mass production readiness for the world's most advanced DRAM technology node. This LPDDR5X mobile memory delivers top speeds of 8.5 gigabits per second, with significant gains in power efficiency (15% improvement) and bit density (over 35% improvement) at 16Gb per die capacity. The 1β node is poised to support highly responsive applications from mobile to data centers and intelligent vehicles, stemming from Micron's pioneering R&D and nanomanufacturing capabilities.

title: Dimensional US Sustainability Core 1 ETF Holdings
summary: This article details the Dimensional US Sustainability Core 1 ETF (DFSU) holdings as of its last reported update. The ETF, created on November 1, 2022, is an actively managed fund focusing on US equities across various market caps with high profitability and positive sustainability. It currently manages $2179.85 million in assets across 1907 holdings, with top investments including NVIDIA Corp, Apple Inc, and Amazon.com Inc.

title: Jaguar Land Rover Secures Semi Conductor Chips For Future Electric Cars
summary: Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) has formed a strategic partnership with Wolfspeed, Inc. to secure Silicon Carbide semiconductors for its next-generation electric vehicles. This collaboration aims to enhance powertrain efficiency and extend driving range for JLR's upcoming electric models, with the first Range Rover vehicles featuring this technology expected in 2024. The partnership is a key part of JLR's "Reimagine" strategy to become carbon net zero by 2039.

title: Lotus’ Super SUV Targets Self-Driving Fast Laps at Racetrack
summary: Lotus' new electric super SUV, the Eletre, aims to be the first car to complete a self-driving lap of Germany's Nürburgring racetrack. This ambitious goal is supported by the vehicle's standard-equipped ROBO Galaxy autonomous driving platform, which includes deployable Lidar technology and two Nvidia Drive Orin systems processing 508 trillion operations per second. While current regulations prevent full autonomous driving on public roads, Lotus plans to demonstrate the Eletre's capabilities at private facilities like the Nürburgring.

title: Take the Green Train: NVIDIA BlueField DPUs Drive Data Center Efficiency
summary: NVIDIA's BlueField DPUs are significantly improving data center efficiency and reducing power consumption. Tests with Ericsson, Red Hat, and VMware showed power reductions of up to 24% and performance increases up to 54x compared to CPUs, by offloading networking, security, and storage tasks. These advancements contribute to substantial cost savings and align with the growing need for green computing solutions.

title: How Taiwan won the semiconductor race
summary: This article explains how Taiwan became a dominant force in the global semiconductor industry, despite starting as an agricultural economy. It attributes Taiwan's success to globalization's impact on electronics, East Asia's skilled workforce and infrastructure, and a unique business model focused on contract manufacturing rather than brand development. The piece highlights TSMC's role in supplying advanced chips globally, creating a significant dependency on Taiwan.

title: Intel Says Its On Track With “Aggressive” 2030 Foundry Goals, Aiming The 2nd Spot By The End of The Decade
summary: Intel is aggressively pursuing its 2030 foundry goals, aiming to become the world's second-largest chip manufacturer, surpassing Samsung and closing in on TSMC. The company is investing significantly in new fabrication plants globally, developing next-gen process technologies, and building capacity to attract clients and diversify the semiconductor supply chain. Intel plans to achieve this through strategic investments, global expansion, and strong competition against its rivals.

title: Chaos Engineering: Unleashing havoc in production
summary: Chaos engineering, a practice pioneered by Netflix, involves intentionally disrupting production environments to identify weaknesses and build system resilience. This approach, likened to "Bootcamp for DevOps teams," helps organizations prepare for inevitable service failures in complex cloud infrastructures. Tools like Chaos Monkey and Chaos Mesh are used to simulate outages, allowing teams to develop robust systems that can recover quickly from disruptions.

title: Tower Semiconductor: Opportunity or risk?
summary: Intel agreed to acquire Tower Semiconductor for $53 per share, but the market fears regulatory hurdles, especially from China and Japan, causing Tower's share price to drop significantly. The deal, valued at $5.4 billion at the time of agreement, needs approvals from multiple countries, including the US, China, Germany, Israel, Japan, the UK, and Italy. Analysts suggest that while regulatory risk exists, particularly with China due to US-China tensions, previous Israeli semiconductor acquisitions ultimately received Chinese approval, and Japan's hesitancy regarding M&A deals might be overcome as Intel plans to maintain operations there.

title: Exclusive: Nvidia offers new advanced chip for China that meets U.S. export controls
summary: Nvidia has developed a new advanced chip, the A800, specifically for the Chinese market, which complies with recent U.S. export control rules designed to restrict cutting-edge technology to China. This move by Nvidia (NVDA.O) is a strategic effort to maintain its presence in the significant Chinese market after U.S. regulations impacted sales of its A100 chip, with the A800 featuring a reduced data transfer rate to meet the export requirements. Analysts suggest this is a "repackaged A100 GPU" demonstrating Nvidia's adaptability to trade restrictions.

title: HPE Expands Supercomputing Portfolio with New HPE Cray EX and XD Systems
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) has expanded its supercomputing portfolio with new HPE Cray EX and HPE Cray XD systems, designed to make high-performance computing more accessible to enterprises. These new systems leverage HPE's exascale innovation to offer enhanced performance and AI-at-scale capabilities in smaller, more energy-efficient form factors and at lower price points. This expansion aims to help various industries, including energy, financial services, health, life sciences, and manufacturing, accelerate R&D, improve time-to-market, and strengthen competitiveness through advanced modeling, simulation, and AI.

title: Nvidia’s new chip is tailored for Chinese market and meets US export regulations
summary: Nvidia has introduced a new A800 GPU specifically designed for the Chinese market to comply with US export regulations, which previously banned sales of its A100 and H100 chips without a license. This move allows Nvidia to continue serving its Chinese customers, who represent about a quarter of its gross sales, while adhering to US government’s restrictions on advanced chip technology. The A800 is an alternative product engineered to meet reduced export control requirements and cannot be programmed to exceed them.

title: ‘Matter’ kicks off with a bang in Amsterdam – with Silicon Labs in starring role
summary: The new 'Matter' IoT standard launched in Amsterdam, featuring Silicon Labs in a prominent role and showcasing new smart home solutions. Silicon Labs, aiming to be "the Nvidia of IoT," predicts 40 billion IoT devices by 2030 and significant growth for smart home IoT due to Matter's interoperability. The standard, backed by nearly three hundred companies, aims to simplify smart home experiences for consumers.

title: Intel debuts powerful Max Series CPUs and GPUs for high-performance computing and AI
summary: Intel has launched its new Max Series CPUs and GPUs, designed to compete in the high-performance computing (HPC) and artificial intelligence (AI) markets against rivals like AMD and Nvidia. These new chips will power the upcoming Aurora supercomputer at Argonne National Laboratory, aiming to make HPC and AI more accessible for solving complex global challenges. Intel claims its Max Series offers significant performance advantages and better power efficiency compared to competitive silicon.

title: Hewlett Packard Enterprise Extends Supercomputing to the Enterprise with New HPE Cray Portfolio
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) is expanding its supercomputing portfolio with new HPE Cray EX and HPE Cray XD supercomputers, making exascale-class technology more accessible and affordable for enterprises. These systems are designed to help businesses across various industries, including energy, finance, healthcare, and manufacturing, accelerate R&D, AI, and machine learning initiatives. The new offerings provide significant performance and AI-at-scale capabilities in smaller form factors, supporting advanced modeling, simulation, and data-intensive workloads in traditional data centers.

title: Innovator Equity Managed Floor ETF Holdings
summary: This article details the holdings of the Innovator Equity Managed Floor ETF (SFLR), which was established on November 9, 2022. The ETF has

title: Innovator Equity Managed Floor ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:SFLR) $SFLR
summary: The Innovator Equity Managed Floor ETF (SFLR) is an ETF that aims to provide capital appreciation by investing in large-cap US stocks while utilizing a laddered options strategy to hedge downside risk, targeting a maximum 10% loss on a rolling 12-month basis. Launched on November 8, 2022, the fund has $1.68 billion in assets under management and a net expense ratio of 0.89%. As of early May 2026, its stock had increased by 2.2% year-to-date and its top holdings include major tech companies like NVIDIA, Apple, and Microsoft.

title: AMD launches data center CPU 'Genoa', taps Google, Microsoft as customers (Nov. 10)
summary: AMD has launched its fourth-generation EPYC processor, codenamed "Genoa," for data centers, securing major customers like Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, and Oracle. This new chip offers significant performance and energy efficiency improvements over its predecessor, translating into lower operational costs for enterprises and cloud data centers. The launch comes as rival Intel faces delays with its own data center chip, and AMD continues to gain market share, boosting its stock by about 14%.

title: Reza Partners with Perfect Corp. to Enable Virtual Try On of Jewelry
summary: French jewelry brand Reza has collaborated with Perfect Corp. to integrate AI and AR virtual try-on technology into its new eCommerce website. This technology, featuring Perfect Corp.'s AgileHand, allows customers to virtually try on rings, earrings, and bracelets in real-time digital renderings. The partnership aims to enhance the luxury accessories shopping experience by providing an immersive and impactful virtual try-on solution.

title: HPE's low-end supercomputers take aim at the AI market
summary: HPE and Dell are introducing new supercomputing and high-performance computing (HPC) systems designed to meet the growing demands of AI-driven workloads. HPE is focusing on smaller, lower-cost supercomputers with advanced cooling, while Dell is enhancing its HPC offerings with powerful GPUs, aiming to make supercomputing capabilities more accessible to a broader range of enterprise users. This convergence of supercomputing and HPC is blurring the lines between the two, as both companies compete to provide infrastructure that can efficiently handle complex AI, modeling, and simulation tasks.

title: NVIDIA H100 and Quantum-2 Systems Announced Worldwide
summary: NVIDIA announced widespread adoption of its H100 Tensor Core GPUs and Quantum-2 InfiniBand, with offerings on Microsoft Azure and over 50 partner systems. The company also released major updates to its cuQuantum, CUDA, and BlueField DOCA acceleration libraries, and expanded Omniverse support for scientific computing. These initiatives aim to accelerate scientific discovery using a comprehensive HPC platform integrating AI and numerical methods.

title: NVIDIA Omniverse Opens Portals for Scientists to Explore Our Universe
summary: NVIDIA announced that its Omniverse platform now supports leading scientific computing visualization software and new batch-rendering workloads on NVIDIA A100 and H100 Tensor Core GPUs. This expansion enables scientists and engineers to use Omniverse for advanced simulations, visualize complex datasets, and create real-time digital twins for various scientific applications. Organizations like Argonne National Laboratory and Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory are already leveraging Omniverse to enhance their research workflows and foster collaboration across global teams.

title: AMD announces its reprogrammable Versal AI chips are ready for space-based deployments
summary: AMD's reprogrammable Versal AI Core chip has achieved Class B qualification, making it suitable for space-based deployments in commercial satellites. This radiation-resistant SoC enables significant advancements in onboard AI processing for satellites, offering greater performance and reconfigurability compared to traditional ASICs. Raytheon Co. is an early adopter, planning to use these chips for its next-generation space processors.

title: Buffett’s Taiwan Semiconductor Stake Highlights Beaten-Down Semi Stocks
summary: Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway has invested $4.1 billion in Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, drawing attention to the semiconductor industry, which Morningstar analysts consider largely undervalued. Following a significant selloff in 2022 due to recession fears and U.S. restrictions on sales to China, many semiconductor companies, including Skyworks Solutions, Teradyne, and Taiwan Semiconductor, are rated as significantly undervalued. The article details Morningstar's perspectives on Nvidia, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, ASML, Broadcom, and Texas Instruments, highlighting investment opportunities despite industry challenges.

title: Industry Ministry, U.S. Firm to Cooperate on Semiconductor Industry Development
summary: Indonesia's Industry Ministry is partnering with a United States company, Zerro Power, co-founded by innovator Sehat Sutardja, to establish an integrated circuit design center. This collaboration aims to reduce Indonesia's dependence on semiconductor imports and develop an independent national semiconductor industry. The initiative is part of broader efforts to secure the semiconductor supply chain amidst increasing global demand.

title: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4080 Graphics Cards Now Available at Newegg.com
summary: Newegg Commerce, Inc. announced the availability of NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4080 graphics cards on Newegg.com. The RTX 4080 boasts significant performance improvements over previous generations, powered by the new NVIDIA Ada Lovelace architecture, and is also offered in pre-built ABS and MSI gaming PCs. Jim Tseng, Newegg's Director of Product Management, anticipates strong customer demand following the successful launch of the RTX 4090.

title: Nvidia and Microsoft partner to build AI supercomputer
summary: Nvidia and Microsoft are collaborating to build one of the world's most powerful AI supercomputers within Microsoft's Azure cloud platform. This partnership involves equipping Azure with tens of thousands of Nvidia's H100 GPUs and Quantum-2 network switches, along with optimizing their respective AI development tools. Nvidia will also expand its use of Azure to support its generative AI research, leveraging the platform to advance technologies like its MT-NLG system.

title: GeForce RTX 4080 Out Now: Beyond Fast For Gamers & Creators
summary: NVIDIA has released the GeForce RTX 4080 graphics card, featuring its 3rd generation RTX architecture, making it available through NVIDIA and various add-in card providers and system integrators. The RTX 4080 offers significant performance improvements over its predecessor, the RTX 3080 Ti, especially in ray-traced games, while maintaining efficient power consumption. It includes advanced features like NVIDIA DLSS 3, dual 8th gen NVIDIA Encoders for video, and AV1 support, enhancing experiences for both gamers and creators.

title: Nvidia says it is working with Microsoft to build 'massive' cloud AI computer
summary: Nvidia Corp is partnering with Microsoft Corp to build a "massive" cloud AI computer on Microsoft's Azure cloud, utilizing thousands of Nvidia's powerful H100 and A100 GPUs. This collaboration aims to handle intense artificial intelligence computing work, driven by the increasing demand for faster processing from AI models. Nvidia will also be a customer of Microsoft's AI cloud computer, developing AI applications for its own services.

title: AMD chip to power auto supplier Aisin’s new automated car parking system
summary: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD) announced that its Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoC microprocessor will power a new automated parking system developed by Japan's Aisin Corp. This system aims to make automated parking more mainstream by offering a cost-effective solution for automakers. The use of AMD's FPGA-based chip, acquired from Xilinx, will allow for post-sale software and chip updates in vehicles, with production expected to begin on 2024 models.

title: Nvidia revenue falls 17% but data center growth remains strong
summary: Nvidia's fiscal third-quarter revenue fell 17% overall but its data center business saw significant growth, up 31% year-over-year. The company's gaming division sales were down 51% due to slowing demand and inventory issues. Despite beating revenue expectations, earnings per share were light, and Nvidia expects gross margin to recover in the current quarter.

title: Chip Maker Nvidia Issues Tepid Earnings Forecast as Videogaming Business Slows
summary: Nvidia Corp. issued a muted earnings outlook and reported a significant decline in quarterly sales, primarily due to decreased consumer demand for its videogaming chips. The company's revenue fell 17% to $5.93 billion in its fiscal third quarter, with gaming-segment sales more than halving. While sales exceeded analyst expectations, net profit at $680 million fell short.

title: Intel FakeCatcher detects deepfakes with a 96% accuracy rate
summary: Intel has launched FakeCatcher, a deepfake detection platform that boasts a 96% accuracy rate and provides real-time results. Unlike other solutions, FakeCatcher identifies genuine human characteristics like subtle blood flow signals in video pixels to distinguish real content from AI-generated fakes. This technology aims to restore trust in media and can be used by news organizations, social media platforms, and non-profit groups to combat the spread of manipulated videos.

title: Lockheed Martin, NVIDIA to Build Digital Twin of Current Global Weather Conditions for the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration
summary: Lockheed Martin and NVIDIA are collaborating to create an AI-driven Earth Observations Digital Twin for the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA). This system will efficiently monitor global environmental conditions, including extreme weather, by fusing data from various space and Earth-based sensors. The project aims to provide NOAA with a high-resolution, accurate, and timely depiction of global conditions to improve weather predictions and understanding of environmental changes.

title: OSS, TMGcore debut a liquid-immersion cooled transportable supercomputer featuring Nvidia GPUs
summary: One Stop Systems (OSS) and TMGcore have collaborated to launch a new two-phase liquid immersion-cooled version of the OSS Rigel Edge Supercomputer, designed for AI Transportable applications. This supercomputer, featuring Nvidia GPUs, offers efficiency, compactness, ruggedness, and high performance by using a unique immersion cooling technology that removes heat through liquid boiling, eliminating the need for fans and heatsinks. This innovation results in a smaller, more robust system with reduced power consumption and noise, ideal for autonomous vehicles, edge computing, and robotic process automation.

title: Nvidia beats revenue estimates, reassures investors
summary: Nvidia reported better-than-expected revenue for the fiscal third quarter, driven by strong demand for its AI and data-center chips, despite a slowdown in the PC market and challenges in China. The company's data center unit saw a 31% sales increase, offsetting a 51% drop in its gaming business. Although the fourth-quarter outlook was slightly below some estimates, it was sufficient to alleviate investor concerns, with CEO Jensen Huang acknowledging ongoing macroeconomic difficulties and COVID-19 restrictions in China.

title: Competition gets heated on Fungible’s DPU patch
summary: Fungible, a data processing unit (DPU) startup founded in 2015, is facing intense competition from major players like AMD, Intel, Kalray, Marvell, and Nvidia. Despite developing impressive DPU chips and acquiring composability software, Fungible has struggled to secure major customers or OEM deals and recently pivoted away from composable systems to focus on its storage technology. The company reportedly tried to raise more funding unsuccessfully and is now in a precarious position amidst rumors of acquisition.

summary: NVIDIA reported Q3 FY23 revenue of $5.9 billion, down 17% year-over-year but still beating analyst estimates due to strong data center sales. While gaming revenue declined significantly from post-pandemic highs, the company saw substantial growth in its data center and automotive segments, indicating a strategic shift and resilience. NVIDIA provided Q4 FY23 revenue guidance of $6 billion, showing confidence in its future despite current macroeconomic challenges and adjustments in the gaming market.

These acquisitions aim to strengthen Ciena's presence in the lucrative broadband access market, which is a growing segment of its overall sales.

summary: Samsung Foundry has reportedly secured orders from major firms like NVIDIA, Qualcomm, IBM, and Baidu to manufacture advanced 3-nanometer chips. summary: Qubit Pharmaceuticals is leveraging hybrid quantum computing, combining classical and quantum computing, to significantly accelerate drug discovery. The company uses NVIDIA's QODA programming model and their Atlas software to simulate drug molecules, aiming to reduce the time and cost of identifying promising treatments for various diseases. This approach seeks to bring down the number of drug compounds needed for preclinical testing, saving substantial time and money in the pharmaceutical development process.

summary: Monarch has begun production of its MK-V, a driver-optional, all-electric tractor, with the first models slated for Constellation Brands. After four years of development and testing, the MK-V will begin shipping by mid-2023 at a price of $68,000, utilizing NVIDIA Jetson Xavier NX chips for its AI and autonomous capabilities. While other companies are also developing autonomous tractors, Monarch aims to be the first with a driver-optional electric model, entering a growing robot-powered agriculture market.

title: PCI-SIG States That Partners Are Responsible For User Safety Following 16-Pin 12VHPWR Cable Lawsuit
summary: PCI-SIG has issued a statement regarding the 16-Pin 12VHPWR cable, emphasizing that its members are responsible for the design, manufacturing, and safety testing of products that use the specification. This response comes after a class-action lawsuit was filed against NVIDIA concerning melting cables on the RTX 4090, which the lawsuit alleges pose a serious electrical and fire hazard. PCI-SIG stresses the importance for all members to take appropriate measures to ensure end-user safety.

title: TSMC to make higher-end chips in US: sources
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC) plans to produce advanced 4-nanometer chips at its new Arizona plant when it opens in 2024, an upgrade from initial plans, following pressure from US customers like Apple. The company is also expected to commit to a second plant for even more advanced 3-nanometer chips. This move aligns with US efforts to bolster domestic semiconductor manufacturing due to supply chain disruptions and geopolitical concerns, though Taiwan intends to keep its latest technology at home.

title: Intel says it will squeeze 1 trillion transistors onto a chip package by 2030
summary: Intel's researchers have revealed innovations in chip packaging that could lead to chips with over a trillion transistors by 2030, significantly extending Moore's Law. This development would result in computer chips ten times more powerful than current advanced silicon. The company aims to address the increasing demand for computing power driven by data consumption and AI.

summary: Lattice Semiconductor has launched Lattice Avant, a new FPGA platform designed to extend its low-power leadership into mid-range FPGAs. This platform offers enhanced power efficiency, advanced connectivity, and optimized computing capabilities, targeting applications in Communications, Computing, Industrial, and Automotive markets. The Avant platform, beginning with the Avant-E family, aims to double Lattice's addressable market and accelerate customer designs with superior power efficiency and performance.

summary: This article explores how artificial intelligence is revolutionizing the world of sports across various domains. title: Deutsche Bank Partners with NVIDIA to embed AI into Financial Services
summary: Deutsche Bank announced a multi-year innovation partnership with NVIDIA to integrate AI and machine learning into financial services. This collaboration aims to accelerate the use of AI for improved risk management, enhanced customer service through interactive avatars, and better extraction of insights from unstructured data. The partnership will support Deutsche Bank's cloud transformation and expand its internal AI center of excellence, focusing on explainable and responsible AI.

summary: Nvidia and Deutsche Bank have announced a multiyear "innovation partnership" to accelerate the use of AI and machine learning in financial services. This collaboration aims to develop regulatory-compliant, AI-powered services, enhance risk model development, and accelerate Deutsche Bank's digital transformation. They will also explore AI for immersive metaverse experiences and advanced data analytics using "Finformers" to identify risks like fraud.

summary: Taiwanese chipmaker TSMC announced it would more than triple its investment in its new Arizona plant to $40 billion, marking one of the largest foreign investments in U.S. history. President Joe Biden praised the project as a move to bring American manufacturing back and strengthen the U.S. supply chain for semiconductors. The expanded investment includes building a second facility for advanced 3-nanometer chips by 2026, aiming to create 13,000 high-tech jobs and address semiconductor shortages.

summary: Jaguar Land Rover has formed a strategic partnership with Wolfspeed to integrate silicon carbide semiconductors into its next-generation electric vehicles. This collaboration aims to enhance powertrain efficiency and extend the driving range of EVs, with the technology first appearing in Range Rover vehicles from 2024 and then in the new all-electric Jaguar brand in 2025. The agreement is part of Jaguar Land Rover's larger strategy to transition to an electric-first business and achieve carbon net-zero operations by 2039.

This achievement marks a lifelong dream for Curran, who plans to ring the NYSE bell in January to celebrate.

summary: Uber Eats has launched autonomous food deliveries in Miami through a partnership with robotics company Cartken, starting in Dadeland and planning further expansion in 2023. summary: Despite significant federal subsidies from the CHIPS Act, major semiconductor manufacturers like Micron Technology, Intel, AMD, Nvidia, and Qualcomm are implementing layoffs or hiring freezes due to slowing demand in key markets. Micron, one of the largest memory chip makers, plans to cut 10% of its workforce, impacting 4,800 employees, citing a "dramatic drop in demand" for PC and smartphone chips. TSMC, a major contract chip manufacturer for companies like Apple, AMD, and Nvidia, plans to develop multiple versions of this technology and is building new fabrication plants in Arizona.

summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) has begun mass production of its most advanced 3-nanometre chips in southern Taiwan, with chairman Mark Liu emphasizing continued investment and capacity expansion on the island. Despite increasing foreign investments, including a significant expansion in Arizona, TSMC assures that the bulk of its manufacturing will remain in Taiwan, demonstrating its commitment to its home base. The company also announced plans for next-generation 2-nanometre chip factories in northern and central Taiwan.

title: Sales of computer graphics cards slump to lowest level in two decades
summary: Sales of computer graphics cards hit a 20-year low in Q3 2022 due to a global economic slowdown and the impact of the Ethereum merge on cryptocurrency mining. Major chipmakers like AMD and Nvidia experienced significant declines in discrete desktop GPU shipments, with AMD particularly hard hit. Despite the slump, new high-end GPU launches and Intel's entry into the market (grabbing a 4% share) offer potential for future sales boosts.

title: TSMC ramps up 3nm chip production in Taiwan
summary: TSMC has officially begun mass production of 3nm chips at its facilities in southern Taiwan, a process expected to offer substantial improvements in density, performance, and power efficiency compared to its 5nm node.
